3DModel: A 3DModel, as a MediaObject under CreativeWork, represents some kind of three-dimensional content, which may have various digital encodings. Also called 3D content, digital model, virtual model. Examples: A CAD file of an engine part, a character model for a video game, a geospatial terrain model, an architectural rendering.
AMRadioChannel: An AMRadioChannel is a specific type of BroadcastChannel that transmits radio signals using amplitude modulation. Also called AM channel, amplitude modulation radio. Examples: WABC 770 AM, KFI 640 AM, BBC Radio 4 LW.
APIReference: APIReference, as a TechArticle under CreativeWork, provides documentation for application programming interfaces. Also called API documentation, developer reference, programming interface guide. Examples: Google Maps API documentation, Stripe API reference, Python `requests` library documentation.
AboutPage: An AboutPage is a specific type of WebPage dedicated to providing information about an organization, person, or entity. Also called About Us page, company info page, profile page. Examples: The "About Us" section of a company website, a personal biography page, a project overview page.
AcceptAction: AcceptAction, as an AllocateAction, is the act of committing to or adopting an object. Also called approve, agree to, take on, embrace. Examples: Accepting a job offer, accepting terms and conditions, accepting a gift, accepting a proposal. Distinct from RejectAction, which is the antonym of committing to an object.
Accommodation: An Accommodation is a Place that can house human beings, such as a hotel room, camping pitch, or meeting room. Also called lodging, dwelling, living space, temporary residence. Examples: A hotel suite, a campsite, a vacation rental apartment, a conference room.
AccountingService: An AccountingService is a LocalBusiness that provides accountancy services. Also called accounting firm, bookkeeping service, tax preparation service. Examples: H&R Block, Deloitte Tax Services, a local CPA firm.
AchieveAction: AchieveAction is an instantaneous Action representing the accomplishment of something through prior efforts. Also called accomplish, attain, succeed, complete. Examples: Winning a race, graduating from college, reaching a sales target, completing a project.
Action: An Action is a fundamental schema.org type representing an activity performed by an agent, potentially involving objects, participants, locations, and instruments, and producing a result. Also called activity, operation, deed, event. Examples: Reading a book, buying groceries, sending an email, cooking dinner.
ActionAccessSpecification: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."
ActionStatusType: ActionStatusType is an Enumeration representing the current state or status of an Action. Also called action state, status of action, progress status. Examples: `ActiveActionStatus`, `CompletedActionStatus`, `FailedActionStatus`, `PotentialActionStatus`.
ActivateAction: ActivateAction, as a ControlAction, is the act of starting or turning on a device or application. Also called turn on, start up, enable, initiate. Examples: Turning on a light, starting a timer, activating an alarm, launching an app. Distinct from DeactivateAction, which is the act of stopping or turning off.
AddAction: AddAction, as an UpdateAction, is the act of editing by incorporating an object into a collection. Also called append, include, insert, attach. Examples: Adding an item to a shopping cart, adding a friend on social media, adding a song to a playlist, adding a comment to a post. Distinct from RemoveAction, which is the act of taking an object out of a collection.
AdministrativeArea: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.
AdultEntertainment: AdultEntertainment is an EntertainmentBusiness specializing in content or services intended for adults. Also called adult venue, adult club, adult establishment. Examples: A strip club, an adult movie theater, an adult bookstore.
AdultOrientedEnumeration: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.
AdvertiserContentArticle: An AdvertiserContentArticle is an Article that has been paid for or produced to the specifications of an external entity. Also called sponsored article, advertorial, native advertising, paid content. Examples: A blog post promoting a product written by an influencer, a sponsored news segment, an article funded by a brand. Distinct from NewsArticle, which is typically produced by independent journalists.
AggregateOffer: An AggregateOffer is an Offer that groups multiple individual offers for the same product or service, often from different merchants. Also called bundled offers, collective offer, multiple offers. Examples: A product page showing prices from several retailers, a flight search result listing different airline prices, a comparison shopping result. Distinct from Offer, which represents a single offer for a product or service.
AggregateRating: An AggregateRating is a Rating that represents the average or summary of multiple individual ratings or reviews. Also called average rating, collective rating, summary score, overall rating. Examples: A product's 4.5-star rating based on 100 reviews, a movie's Rotten Tomatoes score, a restaurant's Yelp rating. Distinct from Rating, which is a single individual rating.
AgreeAction: AgreeAction, as a ReactAction, is the act of expressing a consistency of opinion with an object or proposition. Also called concur, assent, approve, consent. Examples: Agreeing with a statement, consenting to a proposal, approving a plan, liking a social media post. Distinct from DisagreeAction, which is the act of expressing an inconsistency of opinion.
Airline: An Airline is an Organization that provides air transportation services for passengers. Also called air carrier, air transport company, flight operator. Examples: United Airlines, British Airways, Lufthansa, Southwest Airlines. Distinct from Airport, which is the facility where planes take off and land.
Airport: An Airport is a CivicStructure that serves as a facility for aircraft to take off and land, and for passenger and cargo services. Also called airfield, aerodrome, air terminal. Examples: London Heathrow Airport, John F. Kennedy International Airport, Tokyo Narita Airport. Distinct from Airline, which is the company operating flights.
AlignmentObject: An AlignmentObject is an Intangible item describing a relationship or correspondence between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework. Also called learning alignment, competency mapping, educational standard link. Examples: A resource aligned to a specific Common Core State Standard, a course module mapped to a learning outcome, a textbook chapter linked to a curriculum objective.
AllocateAction: AllocateAction, as an OrganizeAction, is the act of assigning resources to tasks, objects, or events. Also called assign, designate, distribute, earmark. Examples: Allocating budget to a project, assigning staff to a task, reserving a room for a meeting, distributing supplies.
AmpStory: An AmpStory is a CreativeWork with a visual storytelling format designed for online viewing, especially on mobile devices. Also called AMP Web Story, visual story, mobile story. Examples: A Google AMP Story about a travel destination, a news publisher's visual story, a brand's product showcase story.
AmusementPark: An AmusementPark is an EntertainmentBusiness offering rides, attractions, and other forms of entertainment. Also called theme park, funfair, carnival. Examples: Disneyland, Six Flags, Universal Studios, Cedar Point.
AnalysisNewsArticle: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.
AnatomicalStructure: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.
AnatomicalSystem: An AnatomicalSystem is a MedicalEntity comprising a group of anatomical structures that function together to perform a specific task. Also called organ system, biological system, body system. Examples: The circulatory system, the digestive system, the nervous system, the skeletal system. Distinct from AnatomicalStructure, which is an individual part of the body.
AnimalShelter: An AnimalShelter is a LocalBusiness that provides temporary housing and care for animals, often facilitating adoption. Also called animal rescue, humane society, pet shelter. Examples: The ASPCA, a local humane society, a dog rescue organization.
Answer: An Answer is a CreativeWork that is a Comment, specifically a response offered to a question. Also called reply, response, solution, explanation. Examples: a student's answer on a test, a user's reply to a forum post, a doctor's diagnosis, a riddle's solution.
Apartment: An Apartment is a self-contained housing unit, a type of residential real estate that occupies only part of a building. Also called flat, condo, dwelling unit, residential unit. Examples: a studio apartment, a two-bedroom flat, a penthouse suite, a loft. Distinct from ApartmentComplex, which is a building containing multiple apartments.
ApartmentComplex: An ApartmentComplex is a Residence consisting of a building or group of buildings containing multiple individual apartment units. Also called residential complex, flat complex, housing estate. Examples: The Grand Apartments, Sunset Towers, a student housing complex, a condominium development. Distinct from Apartment, which is a single housing unit within a complex.
AppendAction: An AppendAction is an InsertAction that specifically involves adding an item to the end of an ordered collection. Also called add to end, suffix, concatenate, tack on. Examples: adding a new item to the end of a shopping list, appending a chapter to a book, adding a new log entry to a file, joining two strings.
ApplyAction: An ApplyAction is an OrganizeAction representing the act of formally requesting to join an organization or receive a service, without a guarantee of acceptance. Also called submit application, make a request, seek admission, bid for. Examples: applying for a job, submitting a college application, applying for a loan, requesting a permit. Distinct from RegisterAction, which implies a successful enrollment or sign-up.
ApprovedIndication: An ApprovedIndication is a MedicalIndication for a therapy that has been formally specified and sanctioned by a regulatory body. Also called sanctioned use, authorized indication, regulatory approval, official use. Examples: FDA-approved use of a drug for a specific disease, a medical device's CE mark for a particular procedure, a vaccine's approved age range.
Aquarium: An Aquarium is a CivicStructure, typically a public facility, where aquatic animals and plants are kept and displayed. Also called public aquarium, marine life center, oceanarium. Examples: Monterey Bay Aquarium, Georgia Aquarium, a local fish exhibit.
ArchiveComponent: An ArchiveComponent is an intangible CreativeWork representing any content within an archive, whether an individual item or a collection, described by specific archival properties. Also called archival item, archival record, archive content, collection item. Examples: a historical letter, a collection of photographs, a government document series, a digital archive file.
ArchiveOrganization: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.
ArriveAction: An ArriveAction is a MoveAction representing the act of an agent reaching a specific destination from a starting location. Also called reach destination, get to, land, pull in. Examples: a plane arriving at the airport, a person reaching home, a package arriving at its delivery point, a train pulling into the station. Distinct from DepartAction, which is the act of leaving a place.
ArtGallery: An ArtGallery is an EntertainmentBusiness that displays and often sells works of art. Also called gallery, art exhibition space, fine art dealer. Examples: The Louvre, a local contemporary art gallery, a commercial art dealership, a pop-up exhibition space.
Artery: An Artery is a Vessel, a type of blood vessel that specifically transports blood away from the heart. Also called blood artery, arterial vessel. Examples: aorta, pulmonary artery, carotid artery, femoral artery. Distinct from Vein, which carries blood towards the heart.
Article: An Article is a CreativeWork, typically a written piece such as a news report, magazine feature, or investigative report. Also called written piece, report, feature, essay, column. Examples: a newspaper article about local politics, a magazine feature on travel, a scientific journal article, a blog post. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a specific type of article published on a blog.
AskAction: An AskAction is a CommunicateAction representing the act of posing a question or requesting a favor from someone. Also called inquire, query, request, solicit. Examples: asking for directions, posing a question in a Q&A forum, requesting help from a colleague, asking for a donation. Distinct from ReplyAction, which is a response to a question or request.
AskPublicNewsArticle: An AskPublicNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that serves as an open call from a news organization, soliciting input, insights, or documentation from the public for reporting purposes. Also called public appeal article, crowdsourced news request, call for information. Examples: a newspaper asking readers for stories about a local event, a news site requesting photos from a natural disaster, a journalist seeking expert opinions on a topic.
AssessAction: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.
AssignAction: An AssignAction is an AllocateAction representing the act of allocating an action, event, or task to a specific person or entity. Also called delegate, allocate, task, designate, appoint. Examples: assigning homework to students, delegating a task to an employee, assigning a case to a lawyer, designating a role in a project.
Atlas: An Atlas is a CreativeWork, typically a collection or bound volume of maps, charts, plates, or tables, illustrating a specific subject or region. Also called map collection, cartographic volume, geographical guide. Examples: a world atlas, a historical atlas, an anatomical atlas, a star chart atlas.
Attorney: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.
Audience: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.
AudioObject: An AudioObject is a MediaObject representing an audio file or recording. Also called audio file, sound recording, sound clip, audio track. Examples: an MP3 song, a podcast episode, a voice memo, a sound effect. Distinct from VideoObject, which contains visual content.
AudioObjectSnapshot: An AudioObjectSnapshot is a specific, byte-for-byte identical version of an AudioObject, where identity is determined by the exact content including embedded metadata. Also called exact audio copy, immutable audio file, audio fingerprint. Examples: a specific version of a song file, a forensic copy of an audio recording, a digitally archived audio track. Distinct from AudioObject, which is the general concept of an audio file, not necessarily a specific, immutable version.
Audiobook: An Audiobook is an AudioObject that is a spoken-word recording of a book or other text. Also called spoken book, recorded book, audio novel. Examples: a narrated version of "Moby Dick", a recorded lecture series, a podcast adaptation of a novel. Distinct from Book, which is the written text itself.
AuthenticateAction: An AuthenticateAction is a ControlAction representing the act of verifying one's identity to gain access to a device or application. Also called log in, sign in, verify identity, authorize access. Examples: logging into a website, unlocking a phone with a password, using a fingerprint scanner to access an app, authenticating with a two-factor code.
AuthorizeAction: An AuthorizeAction is an AllocateAction representing the act of granting permission or approval for an object or action. Also called grant permission, approve, sanction, permit, allow. Examples: authorizing a payment, granting access to a file, approving a request, permitting a user to perform an action. Distinct from AuthenticateAction, which is about verifying identity, whereas AuthorizeAction is about granting permissions after identity is verified.
AutoBodyShop: An AutoBodyShop is an AutomotiveBusiness specializing in repairing the exterior and structural damage of vehicles. Also called car body repair, collision repair shop, panel beater (UK). Examples: Maaco, a local dent repair service, a collision center. Distinct from AutoRepair, which focuses on mechanical issues.
AutoDealer: An AutoDealer is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells new or used vehicles. Also called car dealership, vehicle retailer, auto sales. Examples: a Ford dealership, a used car lot, a luxury car showroom. Distinct from AutoRental, which rents vehicles rather than selling them.
AutoPartsStore: An AutoPartsStore is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells components and accessories for vehicles. Also called car parts shop, automotive supply store, spares shop. Examples: AutoZone, O'Reilly Auto Parts, a local specialty parts store.
AutoRental: An AutoRental is an AutomotiveBusiness that provides vehicles for temporary hire. Also called car hire, vehicle rental agency, rent-a-car. Examples: Hertz, Enterprise Rent-A-Car, a local van rental service. Distinct from AutoDealer, which sells vehicles.
AutoRepair: An AutoRepair is an AutomotiveBusiness that provides mechanical maintenance and repair services for vehicles. Also called car mechanic, garage, auto service center, vehicle workshop. Examples: Jiffy Lube, a local independent mechanic, a dealership service department. Distinct from AutoBodyShop, which focuses on exterior and structural damage.
AutoWash: An AutomotiveBusiness specializing in cleaning vehicles. Also called car wash, vehicle cleaning service, auto detailing. Examples: "Shiny Car Wash", "Speedy Auto Spa", "Eco-Friendly Car Cleaners".
AutomatedTeller: A FinancialService provided by a machine for banking transactions. Also called ATM, cash machine, automated banking machine. Examples: "Bank of America ATM", "Wells Fargo cash machine", "independent ATM kiosk".
AutomotiveBusiness: A LocalBusiness focused on vehicle-related services like repair, sales, or parts. Also called car business, auto service center, vehicle dealership. Examples: "Joe's Auto Repair", "Luxury Car Sales", "Parts 'R' Us". Distinct from AutoWash, which specifically cleans vehicles.
BackgroundNewsArticle: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.
Bakery: A FoodEstablishment that bakes and sells bread, cakes, and pastries. Also called bake shop, patisserie, bread shop. Examples: "The Daily Bread Bakery", "Sweet Delights Patisserie", "Grandma's Oven".
BankAccount: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".
BankOrCreditUnion: A FinancialService provided by an institution that handles money and credit for customers. Also called bank, credit union, financial institution. Examples: "Chase Bank", "Navy Federal Credit Union", "Citibank". Distinct from AutomatedTeller, which is a machine, not an institution.
BarOrPub: A FoodEstablishment that primarily serves alcoholic beverages and often food. Also called bar, pub, tavern, lounge. Examples: "The Green Dragon Pub", "O'Malley's Bar & Grill", "The Corner Taproom". Distinct from Restaurant, which primarily focuses on serving meals.
Barcode: An ImageObject representing a visual, machine-readable code used for identification or data storage. Also called QR code, UPC code, data matrix. Examples: "The barcode on a grocery item", "A QR code for a website link", "A shipping label barcode".
Beach: A CivicStructure consisting of a sandy or pebbly shore by a body of water. Also called seashore, coastline, sandy beach, waterfront. Examples: "Copacabana Beach", "Malibu Beach", "Waikiki Beach".
BeautySalon: A HealthAndBeautyBusiness offering cosmetic treatments for hair, skin, and nails. Also called hair salon, nail salon, spa, beauty parlor. Examples: "Fantastic Sams", "Supercuts", "The Glamour Room".
BedAndBreakfast: A LodgingBusiness offering overnight accommodation and breakfast, typically in a private home. Also called B&B, guesthouse, inn. Examples: "The Cozy Nook B&B", "Seaside Guesthouse", "The Old Mill Inn". Distinct from Hotel, which is a larger commercial establishment.
BedDetails: An Intangible entity providing specific information about the types and quantities of beds available in an accommodation. Also called bed configuration, sleeping arrangements, bed inventory. Examples: "Details for two twin beds and one king bed", "Information on a queen bed with a sofa bed", "Specifics for a bunk bed setup". Distinct from BedType, which is an enumeration of bed categories.
BedType: A QualitativeValue enumeration representing a specific category or style of bed. Also called bed category, bed style, bed size. Examples: "King bed", "Queen bed", "Twin bed", "Sofa bed". Distinct from BedDetails, which describes the quantity and combination of beds.
BefriendAction: An InteractAction representing the act of forming a mutual personal connection with someone. Also called make friends with, become friends, form a friendship. Examples: "Befriending a new colleague", "Making friends with a neighbor", "Forming a bond with a classmate". Distinct from FollowAction, which implies a non-reciprocal connection.
BikeStore: A Store specializing in the sale and repair of bicycles and related accessories. Also called bicycle shop, cycle store, bike shop. Examples: "Performance Bicycle", "REI Co-op (bike section)", "Local Bike Shop".
BioChemEntity: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".
Blog: A CreativeWork representing an online journal or informational website displaying information in reverse chronological order. Also called weblog, online journal, personal blog. Examples: "The Huffington Post blog", "A personal travel blog", "A corporate tech blog". Distinct from BlogPosting, which is an individual entry within a blog.
BlogPosting: An Article that is an individual entry or post published within a blog. Also called blog post, blog entry, weblog post. Examples: "A blog post about new software features", "An article on a travel blog", "A recipe post on a food blog". Distinct from Blog, which is the collection of posts.
BloodTest: A MedicalTest performed on a patient's blood sample to diagnose or monitor health conditions. Also called blood analysis, blood panel, blood work. Examples: "A complete blood count (CBC)", "A cholesterol test", "A glucose tolerance test".
BoardingPolicyType: An Enumeration representing different policies used by airlines for boarding passengers. Also called airline boarding rule, boarding group type, flight boarding policy. Examples: "Zone boarding", "Group boarding", "Priority boarding", "Family boarding".
BoatReservation: A Reservation for travel on a boat, ship, or other water vessel. Also called ferry booking, cruise reservation, boat charter booking. Examples: "A reservation for the Staten Island Ferry", "A booking for a private yacht charter", "A cruise cabin reservation". Distinct from BoatTrip, which describes the journey itself.
BoatTerminal: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".
BoatTrip: A Trip representing a journey taken on a commercial ferry line or similar water transport. Also called ferry journey, boat excursion, water travel. Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.
BodyMeasurementTypeEnumeration: A MeasurementTypeEnumeration listing various dimensions of a person's body, often used for clothing fit. Also called body dimension type, clothing size measurement, anthropometric measurement. Examples: "Chest circumference", "Waist size", "Inseam length", "Shoe size".
BodyOfWater: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.
Bone: An AnatomicalStructure consisting of rigid connective tissue that forms the skeletal structure of a body. Also called skeletal bone, osseous tissue. Examples: "Femur", "Skull bone", "Rib cage", "Vertebra". Distinct from Muscle, which is soft tissue for movement.
Book: A CreativeWork consisting of a written or printed work, typically bound together and protected by a cover. Also called publication, volume, printed matter. Examples: "To Kill a Mockingbird", "The Lord of the Rings", "A textbook on physics". Distinct from BookSeries, which is a collection of books.
BookFormatType: An Enumeration representing the physical or digital publication format of a book. Also called book edition type, publication format, reading format. Examples: "Hardcover", "Paperback", "Ebook", "Audiobook".
BookSeries: A CreativeWorkSeries comprising a sequence of books published as a set or with a common theme. Also called book collection, literary series, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter series", "The Chronicles of Narnia", "A Song of Ice and Fire". Distinct from Book, which is a single volume.
BookStore: A BookStore is a LocalBusiness that sells books and related merchandise. Also called book shop, bookseller, literary retailer. Examples: Barnes & Noble, local independent bookstore, Amazon Books.
BookmarkAction: A BookmarkAction is an OrganizeAction where an agent marks an object for later retrieval or reference. Also called flag action, tag action, label action, mark action. Examples: saving a webpage to favorites, tagging an email, marking a chapter in an e-book.
Boolean: Boolean represents a data type that can only have one of two logical values: true or false. Also called logical value, truth value, binary value. Examples: true, false, 1, 0.
BorrowAction: A BorrowAction is a TransferAction representing the act of temporarily obtaining an object under an agreement to return it at a later date. Also called loan acquisition, temporary possession, rental. Examples: borrowing a library book, renting a car, taking a tool from a friend. Distinct from LendAction, which is the act of giving an object for temporary use.
BowlingAlley: A BowlingAlley is a SportsActivityLocation where people can engage in the sport of bowling. Also called bowling center, bowling lane, ten-pin alley. Examples: AMF Bowling, local bowling alley, a bowling club.
BrainStructure: A BrainStructure is an AnatomicalStructure referring to any part of the soft nervous tissue that serves as the coordinating center for sensation, intellect, and nervous activity. Also called cerebral structure, neural component. Examples: cerebellum, hippocampus, frontal lobe, brainstem.
Brand: A Brand is an Intangible entity representing a name, symbol, or design used by an organization to identify and distinguish its products or services. Also called product line, trademark, label, marque. Examples: Nike, Apple, Coca-Cola, Google.
BreadcrumbList: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList representing a hierarchical navigation path, typically on a website, showing the user's current location relative to the site's structure. Also called navigation path, breadcrumbs, site path. Examples: Home > Products > Electronics > Televisions, Blog > Category > Post Title.
Brewery: A Brewery is a FoodEstablishment that produces beer. Also called beer factory, microbrewery, brewpub. Examples: Guinness Brewery, Sierra Nevada Brewing Co., local craft brewery.
Bridge: A Bridge is a CivicStructure built to span physical obstacles like water, valleys, or roads, facilitating passage. Also called overpass, viaduct, span. Examples: Golden Gate Bridge, Brooklyn Bridge, a pedestrian bridge.
BroadcastChannel: A BroadcastChannel is an Intangible entity representing a specific instance of a BroadcastService within a cable or satellite lineup. Also called TV channel, radio station frequency, media channel. Examples: BBC One, CNN, ESPN, local public radio station.
BroadcastEvent: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.
BroadcastFrequencySpecification: A BroadcastFrequencySpecification is an Intangible entity detailing the frequency in MHz and the modulation used for a particular BroadcastService. Also called frequency details, broadcast parameters, channel specification. Examples: 99.5 FM, 1080 AM, UHF channel 23.
BroadcastService: A BroadcastService is a Service that delivers content via broadcast, either over the air or online. Also called broadcasting service, media transmission service, content delivery service. Examples: a national television network, a satellite radio provider, an internet radio service.
BrokerageAccount: A BrokerageAccount is an InvestmentOrDeposit financial product that allows an investor to deposit funds and place investment orders through a licensed broker. Also called investment account, trading account, stock account. Examples: Fidelity brokerage account, Charles Schwab investment account, E*TRADE account. Distinct from BankAccount, which is for general deposits and withdrawals.
BuddhistTemple: A BuddhistTemple is a PlaceOfWorship dedicated to Buddhist religious practices and ceremonies. Also called pagoda, wat, vihara, dharma center. Examples: Wat Arun, Todai-ji Temple, a local Zen center.
BusOrCoach: A BusOrCoach is a Vehicle designed to carry multiple passengers, with coaches being luxury versions for long-distance travel. Also called omnibus, motorcoach, passenger bus, tour bus. Examples: city bus, Greyhound coach, school bus, double-decker bus.
BusReservation: A BusReservation is a Reservation for travel on a bus, providing details about a confirmed booking. Also called bus ticket booking, coach reservation, seat booking. Examples: a confirmed ticket for a cross-country bus trip, a booking for a city tour bus. Distinct from Offer, which is for available tickets, not a specific booking.
BusStation: A BusStation is a CivicStructure serving as a central terminal where buses depart, arrive, and transfer passengers. Also called bus terminal, coach station, bus depot. Examples: Port Authority Bus Terminal, Victoria Coach Station, a local intercity bus station. Distinct from BusStop, which is a smaller, temporary stopping point.
BusStop: A BusStop is a CivicStructure designated as a place where buses regularly pick up and drop off passengers. Also called bus halt, bus stand, transit stop. Examples: a street corner bus stop, a designated stop on a campus route. Distinct from BusStation, which is a larger terminal facility.
BusTrip: A BusTrip is a Trip taken on a commercial bus line. Also called bus journey, coach trip, bus travel. Examples: a cross-country bus journey, a daily commute by bus, a sightseeing bus tour.
BusinessAudience: A BusinessAudience is an Audience defined by characteristics relevant to businesses, such as their industry, size, or role in the value chain. Also called B2B audience, corporate audience, professional audience. Examples: small business owners, IT managers, marketing executives, manufacturing companies. Distinct from PeopleAudience, which targets individual consumers.
BusinessEntityType: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.
BusinessEvent: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.
BusinessFunction: A BusinessFunction is an Enumeration specifying the type of activity or access rights offered by an organization through an offer. Also called commercial activity, service type, transaction type. Examples: Sell, LeaseOut, Repair, ProvideService, Buy.
BuyAction: A BuyAction is a TradeAction representing the act of an agent acquiring goods or services from a seller in exchange for money. Also called purchase action, acquire action, procure action. Examples: buying groceries, purchasing a movie ticket, subscribing to a service. Distinct from SellAction, which is the act of giving goods or services for money.
CDCPMDRecord: A CDCPMDRecord is a StructuredValue representing a record in the CDC tabular data format used for hospital data reporting, specifically for COVID-19 related data. Also called CDC hospital data record, COVID-19 data record. Examples: a daily hospital bed occupancy report, a weekly ICU patient count record.
CableOrSatelliteService: A CableOrSatelliteService is a Service that provides access to media programming, such as TV or radio, delivered via cable or satellite infrastructure. Also called pay TV service, satellite radio provider, broadcast subscription service. Examples: Comcast Xfinity, DirecTV, SiriusXM Satellite Radio.
CafeOrCoffeeShop: A CafeOrCoffeeShop is a FoodEstablishment primarily serving coffee, other beverages, and often light meals or pastries. Also called coffee house, coffee bar, cafe. Examples: Starbucks, local independent coffee shop, a small bistro. Distinct from Restaurant, which typically offers a wider range of full meals.
Campground: A Campground is a CivicStructure or place used for overnight outdoor stays, typically containing multiple individual camping pitches for tents or recreational vehicles. Also called camping site, campsite, RV park, caravan park. Examples: Yellowstone National Park Campground, KOA Campground, a local state park campsite. Distinct from Hotel, which provides indoor lodging.
CampingPitch: An individual outdoor space for overnight stay, typically part of a larger camping site or campground. Also called tent pitch, RV pitch, caravan pitch, campsite spot. Examples: Tent site #3 at Yosemite, RV spot at KOA, a designated area for a caravan. Distinct from Campground, which is the larger site containing multiple pitches.
Canal: An artificial waterway constructed for navigation, irrigation, or drainage. Also called waterway, artificial channel, navigation channel. Examples: Panama Canal, Suez Canal, Erie Canal, Grand Canal of China.
CancelAction: The act of asserting that a future event or action will no longer occur. Also called call off, revoke, annul, abort. Examples: Cancelling a flight, cancelling a meeting, cancelling a subscription. Distinct from ConfirmAction, which is asserting an event will happen.
Car: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle primarily used for personal transportation. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto, vehicle. Examples: Toyota Camry, Ford F-150, Tesla Model 3, Honda Civic.
CarUsageType: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.
Casino: A local business primarily offering gambling activities and often entertainment. Also called gambling house, gaming establishment, resort casino. Examples: Bellagio, Caesars Palace, Monte Carlo Casino.
CategoryCode: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.
CategoryCodeSet: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.
CatholicChurch: A place of worship specifically for the Catholic Christian denomination. Also called Roman Catholic church, Catholic parish, Catholic cathedral. Examples: St. Patrick's Cathedral, Notre Dame de Paris, Basilica of St. Peter. Distinct from Church, which is a general place of Christian worship.
Cemetery: A civic structure designated as a burial ground for the deceased. Also called graveyard, burial ground, memorial park, necropolis. Examples: Arlington National Cemetery, Père Lachaise Cemetery, a local municipal cemetery.
Certification: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.
CertificationStatusEnumeration: An enumeration defining the possible statuses of a certification. Also called certification state, approval status, credential status. Examples: Active, Inactive, Expired, Pending.
Chapter: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.
CheckAction: The act of an agent inspecting, investigating, or examining an object's accuracy, quality, or condition. Also called verify, inspect, examine, audit, review. Examples: Checking a document for errors, checking a car's oil level, checking a patient's vital signs.
CheckInAction: The act of an agent communicating their arrival and confirming a previously reserved service or place. Also called register arrival, confirm reservation, sign in. Examples: Checking into a hotel, checking in for a flight, checking in at a conference. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is simply arriving without prior reservation confirmation.
CheckOutAction: The act of an agent communicating their departure from a previously reserved service or place. Also called depart, sign out, settle bill. Examples: Checking out of a hotel, checking out of a library book, checking out from a rental car service. Distinct from DepartAction, which is simply leaving without prior service completion.
CheckoutPage: A specific type of web page dedicated to completing a purchase or transaction. Also called payment page, order confirmation page, shopping cart page. Examples: The final step of an e-commerce purchase, a page to finalize a booking, a donation payment page.
ChemicalSubstance: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.
ChildCare: A local business providing care and supervision for children. Also called daycare center, nursery school, preschool, creche. Examples: Bright Horizons, a local family daycare, a Montessori preschool.
ChildrensEvent: An event specifically organized and designed for children. Also called kids' event, family event, youth gathering. Examples: A puppet show, a children's birthday party, a school play, a kids' festival.
ChooseAction: The act of expressing a preference or making a selection from a set of options. Also called select, pick, opt for, decide. Examples: Choosing a meal from a menu, choosing a candidate in an election, choosing a color for a car.
Church: A civic structure serving as a place of worship for Christian congregations. Also called house of God, chapel, sanctuary, temple (Christian context). Examples: Westminster Abbey, a local Baptist church, a small village chapel. Distinct from PlaceOfWorship, which is a general term for any religious building.
City: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.
CityHall: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.
CivicStructure: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.
Claim: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.
ClaimReview: A creative work that provides a fact-checking review of a specific claim. Also called fact-check, debunking, truth verification. Examples: A Snopes article debunking a viral claim, a PolitiFact rating of a politician's statement. Distinct from Review, which is a general assessment of an item.
Class: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.
Clip: A short segment or part of a larger audio or video program. Also called segment, excerpt, snippet, short video. Examples: A news clip, a movie trailer, a highlight reel from a sports game, a sound bite. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is the broader category for any creative content.
ClothingStore: A local business specializing in the retail sale of apparel and accessories. Also called apparel store, boutique, fashion shop, garment retailer. Examples: H&M, Zara, Nordstrom, a local boutique. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.
Code: Computer programming source code, such as full solutions, snippets, scripts, or templates. Also called programming code, software code, source program. Examples: Python script, Java application, HTML template, SQL query.
Collection: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.
CollectionPage: A web page specifically designed to display a collection of items. Also called gallery page, catalog page, archive page. Examples: An e-commerce category page, a photo gallery page, a blog post archive page. Distinct from WebPage, which is a general web document.
CollegeOrUniversity: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.
ComedyClub: A local business venue primarily dedicated to hosting comedy performances. Also called stand-up club, humor venue, comedy theater. Examples: The Comedy Store, Caroline's on Broadway, Second City, The Laugh Factory. Distinct from EntertainmentBusiness, which is a broader category for businesses providing entertainment.
ComedyEvent: An event featuring comedic performances or content. Also called stand-up show, humor performance, comedy festival. Examples: A stand-up comedy show, a sketch comedy performance, a comedy festival, an improv night. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.
ComicCoverArt: The visual artwork specifically featured on the cover of a comic book or issue. Also called comic book cover, graphic novel cover, comic art. Examples: The cover of Action Comics #1, a variant cover for a Marvel comic, a graphic novel's front illustration. Distinct from ComicStory, which refers to any indivisible, re-printable unit of a comic, including interior stories.
ComicIssue: An individual, serially published installment of a comic series, uniquely identified by its series name, volume, issue number, and variant description. Also called comic book, comic installment, single issue comic. Examples: The Amazing Spider-Man #1, Detective Comics Vol. 2 #27, Saga #50, a one-shot comic. Distinct from ComicSeries, which is the overarching publication title.
ComicSeries: A sequential publication of comic stories released under a consistent unifying title. Also called comic book series, graphic novel series, comic strip series. Examples: The Walking Dead, Batman, X-Men, Calvin and Hobbes. Distinct from ComicIssue, which is a single installment within the series.
ComicStory: Any indivisible, re-printable unit within a comic, encompassing interior narratives, covers, and backmatter. Also called comic narrative, comic segment, comic content. Examples: The main story in a comic book, a short backup story, a comic book cover, an editorial page. Distinct from ComicCoverArt, which is specifically the artwork on the cover.
Comment: A textual remark or observation made about an item, such as a blog post. Also called remark, feedback, note, annotation. Examples: A user's comment on a YouTube video, a review on a product page, a blog post comment, a code comment.
CommentAction: The act of creating or submitting a comment about a particular subject. Also called commenting, posting a comment, providing feedback. Examples: Writing a review, replying to a forum post, adding a note to a document, leaving a social media comment. Distinct from Comment, which is the content itself.
CommunicateAction: The act of transmitting information to another person or entity through a specific medium. Also called communication, conveying information, interacting. Examples: Sending an email, making a phone call, giving a speech, writing a letter. Distinct from InteractAction, which is a broader category of actions involving interaction.
CompleteDataFeed: A data feed whose standard representation includes all current items, allowing older entries to be safely discarded upon refresh. Also called full data feed, comprehensive feed, complete item feed. Examples: An Atom feed of "Top Twenty Records" where all current records are present, a product catalog feed that always contains all available products, a news feed that provides all current articles. Distinct from DataFeed, which is a general feed that might only contain updates or partial information.
CompoundPriceSpecification: A price specification that combines multiple prices applicable for different dimensions of consumption. Also called bundled price, multi-component price, composite pricing. Examples: A utility bill with separate charges for electricity and water, a rental agreement with base rent and a "final cleaning" fee, a software license with per-user and per-feature costs. Distinct from PriceSpecification, which is a general description of a price.
ComputerLanguage: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.
ComputerStore: A local business specializing in the retail sale of computers and related equipment. Also called PC store, electronics store, computer shop. Examples: Best Buy, Apple Store, a local computer repair and sales shop, Micro Center. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.
ConferenceEvent: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.
ConfirmAction: The act of notifying someone that a future event or action is expected to proceed as planned. Also called confirmation, affirming, verifying, acknowledging. Examples: Confirming a flight reservation, accepting a meeting invitation, acknowledging receipt of an order, confirming an appointment. Distinct from CancelAction, which is the antonym, indicating an event will not happen.
Consortium: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.
ConstraintNode: An intangible type supporting use cases where a node in a structured data graph describes properties that indicate sets of possible values rather than single, exact values. Also called constraint object, abstract node, descriptive node. Examples: A node describing a range of acceptable temperatures, a node specifying a set of required skills, a node defining a minimum and maximum quantity.
ConsumeAction: The act of ingesting or utilizing information, resources, or food. Also called consumption, utilizing, ingesting, using. Examples: Reading a book, eating a meal, watching a movie, using electricity. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.
ContactPage: A web page specifically designed to provide contact information for an entity. Also called contact us page, inquiry page, reach us page. Examples: A website's "Contact Us" page, a business's support page, a personal portfolio's contact section. Distinct from WebPage, which is a general web document.
ContactPoint: A specific point of contact for an organization or person, such as a customer service department. Also called contact information, communication channel, service point. Examples: A customer support phone number, an email address for sales, a physical address for returns, a social media handle. Distinct from ContactPointOption, which is an enumerated option related to a contact point.
ContactPointOption: An enumerated option that describes a specific characteristic or service available at a ContactPoint. Also called contact option, communication preference, service feature. Examples: TollFree, HearingImpairedSupported, Available24Hours. Distinct from ContactPoint, which is the actual point of contact itself.
Continent: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.
ControlAction: An action where an agent operates or manages a device or application. Also called controlling, operating, managing, manipulating. Examples: Turning on a light, adjusting a thermostat, launching a software application, steering a car. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.
ConvenienceStore: A local business retail store offering a limited range of everyday items, often with extended hours. Also called corner store, mini-mart, quick shop. Examples: 7-Eleven, Circle K, a local neighborhood market, a gas station store. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.
Conversation: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.
CookAction: The act of preparing or producing food through cooking processes. Also called cooking, food preparation, culinary action, baking. Examples: Baking a cake, frying an egg, grilling a steak, boiling pasta. Distinct from CreateAction, which is a broader category for making something.
Cooperative: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.
Corporation: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.
CorrectionComment: A CorrectionComment is a specific type of comment that provides corrections or amendments to a CreativeWork. Also called erratum, amendment, revision note. Examples: A correction notice on an online article, an errata sheet for a book, a revised caption for an image.
Country: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.
Course: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. Also called educational program, curriculum, study program, academic course. Examples: "Introduction to Python Programming," "Art History 101," "Advanced Calculus," "Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from CourseInstance, which is a specific offering of a course at a particular time and place.
CourseInstance: A CourseInstance is a specific offering of an educational course, distinguished by its particular time, location, medium, or target student group. Also called course section, class session, course offering, specific class. Examples: "Fall 2023 Introduction to Python (Online)," "Spring 2024 Art History 101 (Campus A, Section B)," "Summer Intensive Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from Course, which is the general description of the educational content.
Courthouse: A Courthouse is a government building where legal cases are heard and judicial proceedings take place. Also called court building, hall of justice, judicial building. Examples: Supreme Court of the United States, Old Bailey, local county courthouse.
CoverArt: CoverArt is the visual artwork displayed on the outer surface of a CreativeWork, such as a book, album, or magazine. Also called album cover, book jacket, magazine cover, artwork. Examples: The cover of "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band," the dust jacket of "To Kill a Mockingbird," the poster for a movie.
CovidTestingFacility: A CovidTestingFacility is a medical clinic or other designated location where individuals can receive testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease. Also called COVID test site, coronavirus testing center, SARS-CoV-2 testing facility. Examples: A drive-thru COVID testing center, a pharmacy offering COVID tests, a hospital's dedicated testing unit.
CreateAction: A CreateAction is the act of deliberately producing, generating, or building a new result or entity by an agent. Also called production, generation, fabrication, construction. Examples: Writing a book, composing a song, building a house, designing a website.
CreativeWork: A CreativeWork is the most generic type of intellectual or artistic creation, encompassing a wide range of media and forms. Also called artistic work, intellectual property, creation, content. Examples: A novel, a film, a photograph, a piece of software, a song, a painting.
CreativeWorkSeason: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.
CreativeWorkSeries: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.
Credential: A Credential is a certificate or document used to verify the identity, qualifications, or authority of a person or entity. Also called certificate, qualification, accreditation, license, identification. Examples: A driver's license, a university degree, a professional certification, a digital security certificate.
CreditCard: A CreditCard is a financial product representing a card payment method that allows users to borrow funds up to a limit for purchases or cash advances. Also called charge card, plastic money, credit account. Examples: Visa, MasterCard, American Express, Discover, JCB.
Crematorium: A Crematorium is a civic structure where human remains are cremated. Also called crematory, funeral pyre facility. Examples: Golders Green Crematorium, a local funeral home with cremation services.
CriticReview: A CriticReview is a professionally written and in-depth evaluation of a creative work, product, or service, published by a recognized reviewing source. Also called professional review, expert review, critical assessment, published critique. Examples: A movie review by a film critic, a restaurant review in a food guide, a book review in a literary magazine. Distinct from UserReview, which is a casual review written by a customer or general user.
CssSelectorType: CssSelectorType is a data type representing a string of text that functions as a CSS selector. Also called CSS selector string, stylesheet selector. Examples: `div.container p`, `#main-content > h1`, `[data-attribute="value"]`.
CurrencyConversionService: A CurrencyConversionService is a financial service that facilitates the exchange of funds from one currency to another. Also called foreign exchange service, money exchange, currency exchange. Examples: A bank's foreign exchange desk, an online currency converter, a travel money service.
DDxElement: A DDxElement is an alternative, closely-related medical condition considered during differential diagnosis, along with the distinguishing signs. Also called differential diagnosis item, alternative diagnosis, rule-out condition. Examples: Considering "strep throat" as a DDxElement for a patient presenting with a sore throat and fever, alongside "common cold."
DENonprofitType: DENonprofitType is an enumeration representing specific types of non-profit organizations recognized under German fiscal code, article 52. Also called German non-profit classification, AO 52 non-profit. Examples: A German charitable foundation, a registered German association for public benefit.
DanceEvent: A DanceEvent is a social gathering or organized occasion primarily focused on dancing. Also called dance party, ball, disco, social dance. Examples: A salsa night, a wedding reception with dancing, a school prom, a folk dance festival.
DanceGroup: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.
DataCatalog: A DataCatalog is a collection or repository of datasets, often providing metadata and access information for each. Also called data repository, dataset collection, data portal. Examples: A government open data portal, a university research data catalog, a scientific data archive.
DataDownload: A DataDownload is a downloadable file or portion of a Dataset, making the data accessible for retrieval. Also called downloadable data, data file, dataset download. Examples: A CSV file of economic statistics, a ZIP archive of research images, a JSON file containing survey results.
DataFeed: A DataFeed is a continuous stream or single file of structured information, typically updated regularly, about one or more entities or topics. Also called RSS feed, Atom feed, data stream, information feed. Examples: A news RSS feed, a stock market data feed, a product inventory feed, a weather data API.
DataFeedItem: A DataFeedItem is an individual entry or record contained within a larger DataFeed. Also called feed entry, feed item, data record. Examples: A single news article in an RSS feed, one product listing in an inventory feed, a single weather observation in a data stream.
DataType: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.
Dataset: A Dataset is a structured collection of information or data, typically organized for analysis or use. Also called data collection, data compilation, data repository. Examples: A spreadsheet of sales figures, a database of customer information, a collection of scientific measurements. Distinct from DataCatalog, which is a collection of multiple datasets.
Date: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".
DateTime: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.
DatedMoneySpecification: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.
DayOfWeek: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.
DaySpa: A local business offering health and beauty services, typically without overnight accommodation. Also called Spa, beauty spa, wellness center. Examples: "The Serene Spa", "Urban Retreat Day Spa", "Relaxation Station". Distinct from HealthClub, which focuses more on fitness and exercise facilities.
DeactivateAction: An action that involves stopping or turning off a device, application, or process. Also called Turn off, disable, shut down, stop. Examples: Turning off a light, deactivating an alarm, stopping a timer, disabling a software feature. Distinct from ActivateAction, which is the act of starting or enabling something.
DefenceEstablishment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.
DefinedRegion: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.
DefinedTerm: An intangible entity representing a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, often used in glossaries or classification schemes. Also called Glossary entry, vocabulary term, classification code, concept. Examples: "ISBN" (International Standard Book Number), "HTTP" (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), "Organic" (as a food label). Distinct from DefinedTermSet, which is a collection of such terms.
DefinedTermSet: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.
DeleteAction: An update action that involves removing an object or item from a recipient or collection. Also called Remove, erase, discard, eliminate. Examples: Deleting an email, removing a contact from an address book, deleting a file from a computer, unpublishing a blog post. Distinct from CreateAction, which is the act of adding something new.
DeliveryChargeSpecification: A price specification detailing the cost associated with delivering an offer using a particular method. Also called Shipping cost, delivery fee, freight charge, postage cost. Examples: "Standard shipping: $5.99", "Express delivery: $15.00", "Free delivery for orders over $50". Distinct from DeliveryMethod, which describes the method itself, not its cost.
DeliveryEvent: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.
DeliveryMethod: An enumeration describing a standardized procedure for transferring a product or service to a customer's chosen destination. Also called Shipping method, fulfillment method, delivery option, shipping carrier. Examples: Mail, freight, direct download, in-store pickup, UPS, FedEx. Distinct from DeliveryChargeSpecification, which specifies the cost of a delivery method.
Demand: An intangible entity representing a public announcement by an organization or person seeking specific goods or services. Also called Request for goods, wanted ad, procurement request, call for bids. Examples: A company seeking bids for a new IT system, a person looking to buy a specific vintage car, a job posting for a software engineer. Distinct from Offer, which is an announcement to provide goods or services.
Dentist: A local business providing dental care services. Also called Dental clinic, dental practice, orthodontist, periodontist. Examples: "Smile Bright Dental", "Dr. Smith's Family Dentistry", "Downtown Orthodontics". Distinct from Physician, who provides general medical care.
DepartAction: A move action representing the act of an agent leaving a specific location to travel towards a destination. Also called Leave, set off, embark, exit. Examples: A plane departing from an airport, a person leaving their home for work, a ship sailing from a port. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is the act of reaching a destination.
DepartmentStore: A type of store that sells a wide variety of consumer goods across different departments. Also called Retail department store, general merchandise store. Examples: Macy's, Nordstrom, Harrods, Kohl's. Distinct from Store, which is a general category for any retail establishment.
DepositAccount: A type of bank account primarily used for depositing funds, often to earn interest or other benefits. Also called Savings account, checking account, current account, money market account. Examples: A personal savings account, a business checking account, a certificate of deposit (CD). Distinct from LoanOrCredit, which represents borrowed funds.
DiagnosticLab: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.
DiagnosticProcedure: A medical procedure primarily performed to identify or confirm a disease or condition, rather than to treat it. Also called Medical test, diagnostic test, screening procedure, examination. Examples: MRI scan, blood test, biopsy, X-ray, colonoscopy. Distinct from TherapeuticProcedure, which is performed for treatment purposes.
Diet: A creative work outlining a strategy for regulating food intake to achieve a specific health or fitness goal. Also called Eating plan, nutritional regimen, dietary program, meal plan. Examples: The Mediterranean diet, a ketogenic diet, a low-sodium diet, a vegan diet. Distinct from NutritionInformation, which provides factual data about food content.
DietarySupplement: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.
DigitalDocument: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.
DigitalDocumentPermission: An intangible entity defining the access rights granted to a specific person or group for a particular digital document. Also called File permission, access control, document rights, sharing setting. Examples: "Read-only access for John Doe", "Edit permission for the Marketing Team", "View and comment access for all users". Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermissionType, which is an enumeration of possible permission types.
DigitalDocumentPermissionType: An enumeration representing a specific type of permission that can be granted for accessing a digital document. Also called Access level, permission role, document access type. Examples: ReadPermission, WritePermission, SharePermission, CommentPermission. Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermission, which is an instance of a permission granted to a specific entity.
DigitalPlatformEnumeration: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.
DisagreeAction: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.
DiscoverAction: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.
DiscussionForumPosting: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.
DislikeAction: A react action expressing a negative sentiment or disapproval towards an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express dislike, disapprove of, show aversion, downvote. Examples: Disliking a movie, expressing disapproval of a policy, downvoting a comment online. Distinct from LikeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or approval.
Distance: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".
Distillery: A Distillery is a FoodEstablishment that produces alcoholic beverages through distillation. Also called liquor producer, spirits manufacturer, alcohol plant. Examples: Jack Daniel's Distillery, The Macallan Distillery, Absolut Vodka Distillery. Distinct from Brewery, which produces beer through fermentation.
DonateAction: DonateAction is a TransferAction representing the act of providing goods, services, or money without expecting compensation, typically for charitable or philanthropic purposes. Also called giving, contributing, gifting, charity. Examples: Donating blood, contributing to a relief fund, gifting clothes to a shelter, volunteering time. Distinct from SellAction, which involves transferring ownership for compensation.
DoseSchedule: A DoseSchedule is a MedicalIntangible specifying a particular regimen for administering a drug or supplement. Also called dosing regimen, medication schedule, treatment plan. Examples: "Take one pill daily", "Apply twice a day for 7 days", "Administer 500mg every 8 hours".
DownloadAction: DownloadAction is a TransferAction representing the act of retrieving an object from a remote source to a local system. Also called fetching, acquiring, pulling. Examples: Downloading a software update, saving a document from the cloud, getting a movie file, retrieving an email attachment.
DrawAction: DrawAction is a CreateAction representing the act of producing a visual or graphical representation of an object, typically using instruments like a pen or pencil on paper. Also called sketching, illustrating, rendering. Examples: Drawing a portrait, sketching a landscape, illustrating a diagram, creating a blueprint.
Drawing: A Drawing is a CreativeWork that is a picture or diagram made with a pencil, pen, or crayon, as opposed to paint. Also called sketch, illustration, diagram, rendering. Examples: A charcoal portrait, a pen-and-ink landscape, a technical blueprint, a child's crayon drawing.
DrinkAction: DrinkAction is a ConsumeAction representing the act of swallowing liquids. Also called imbibing, sipping, quaffing. Examples: Drinking water, sipping coffee, consuming a soft drink, taking a shot of medicine.
DriveWheelConfigurationValue: A DriveWheelConfigurationValue is a QualitativeValue indicating which roadwheels of a vehicle receive torque. Also called drivetrain type, wheel drive configuration. Examples: AllWheelDriveConfiguration, FrontWheelDriveConfiguration, RearWheelDriveConfiguration.
Drug: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.
DrugClass: A DrugClass is a MedicalEntity representing a category of medical drugs, grouped by general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, or physiological effects. Also called drug category, medication group, therapeutic class. Examples: Statins, Antibiotics, Antidepressants, Beta-blockers.
DrugCost: A DrugCost is a MedicalEntity representing the cost per unit of a medical drug, typically referring to wholesale or average retail cost, not an offer price. Also called medication price, pharmaceutical expense, drug expenditure. Examples: Average retail cost of a prescription, wholesale price of a vaccine, maximum reimbursable cost for a generic drug.
DrugCostCategory: A DrugCostCategory is a MedicalEnumeration of predefined categories for medical drug costs. Also called medication cost type, pharmaceutical pricing category. Examples: Retail, Wholesale, Reimbursement.
