DrugLegalStatus: A DrugLegalStatus is a MedicalIntangible indicating the legal availability status of a medical drug. Also called medication legal standing, pharmaceutical regulatory status. Examples: PrescriptionOnly, OverTheCounter, ControlledSubstance.
DrugPregnancyCategory: A DrugPregnancyCategory is a MedicalEnumeration assessing the risk of fetal injury from a drug used by the mother during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy risk category, fetal risk classification. Examples: PregnancyCategoryA, PregnancyCategoryX, PregnancyCategoryD.
DrugPrescriptionStatus: A DrugPrescriptionStatus is a MedicalEnumeration indicating whether a drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter. Also called medication availability, prescription requirement. Examples: PrescriptionOnly, OverTheCounter.
DrugStrength: A DrugStrength is a MedicalIntangible representing a specific potency in which a medical drug is available in a particular country. Also called medication dosage, pharmaceutical concentration. Examples: "500 mg tablets", "10 mg/mL solution", "25 mcg patch".
DryCleaningOrLaundry: A DryCleaningOrLaundry is a LocalBusiness that provides dry-cleaning or laundry services. Also called laundromat, dry cleaner, laundry service. Examples: A local dry cleaner, a self-service laundromat, a commercial laundry facility.
Duration: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).
EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration: An EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration listing the EU energy efficiency classes A-G, A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369. Also called EU energy rating, European energy class. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA+++, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryG.
EatAction: EatAction is a ConsumeAction representing the act of swallowing solid objects. Also called consuming food, dining, ingesting. Examples: Eating a meal, consuming a snack, having dinner, biting into an apple.
EducationEvent: An EducationEvent is an Event focused on learning or instruction. Also called educational activity, learning event, training session. Examples: A university lecture, a workshop on coding, a seminar on financial literacy, a school field trip.
EducationalAudience: An EducationalAudience is an Audience specifically targeted for educational content or programs. Also called student group, learner demographic, academic audience. Examples: K-12 students, university undergraduates, adult learners, professional development participants.
EducationalOccupationalCredential: An EducationalOccupationalCredential is a CreativeWork representing a diploma, academic degree, certification, qualification, or badge awarded to an entity meeting specific requirements. Also called degree, certificate, qualification, license. Examples: A Bachelor of Science degree, a Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, a high school diploma, a professional license.
EducationalOccupationalProgram: An EducationalOccupationalProgram is an Intangible program offered by an institution that defines the learning path to achieve an outcome, such as a credential or new occupational opportunity. Also called academic program, training course, career pathway. Examples: A Master's degree program in engineering, a vocational training program for electricians, a coding bootcamp, a nursing school curriculum.
EducationalOrganization: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.
Electrician: An Electrician is a HomeAndConstructionBusiness specializing in electrical installation and repair services. Also called electrical contractor, wiring specialist. Examples: A local electrician offering home wiring services, a company specializing in commercial electrical installations, an emergency electrician.
ElectronicsStore: An ElectronicsStore is a Store that sells electronic goods. Also called tech shop, gadget retailer, consumer electronics store. Examples: Best Buy, Apple Store, a local computer shop, a mobile phone retailer.
ElementarySchool: An ElementarySchool is an EducationalOrganization providing primary education. Also called primary school, grade school. Examples: Oakwood Elementary School, P.S. 123, a local junior school.
EmailMessage: An EmailMessage is a CreativeWork representing a message sent via electronic mail. Also called email, electronic mail, e-message. Examples: A business correspondence email, a personal email to a friend, a newsletter subscription email, a spam message.
Embassy: An Embassy is a GovernmentBuilding representing the diplomatic mission of one country in another. Also called consulate, diplomatic mission, high commission. Examples: The U.S. Embassy in London, the French Embassy in Washington D.C., a country's consulate general.
EmergencyService: An EmergencyService is a LocalBusiness providing immediate assistance in urgent situations. Also called emergency response, crisis service. Examples: A fire station, an emergency room, a police department, an ambulance service.
EmployeeRole: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.
EmployerAggregateRating: An EmployerAggregateRating is an AggregateRating representing a collective assessment of an Organization's performance as an employer. Also called company rating, employer review score, workplace satisfaction rating. Examples: Glassdoor's overall rating for a company, an average employee satisfaction score, a composite rating from multiple employee surveys.
EmployerReview: An EmployerReview is a Review of an Organization specifically regarding its role as an employer, written by a current or former employee. Also called company review, workplace review, employee testimonial. Examples: A former employee's review of a company's culture, a current employee's feedback on management, a detailed assessment of benefits and work-life balance.
EmploymentAgency: An EmploymentAgency is a LocalBusiness that helps individuals find jobs and employers find suitable candidates. Also called recruitment agency, staffing firm, job placement service. Examples: A temporary staffing agency, an executive search firm, a headhunting company.
EndorseAction: EndorseAction is a ReactAction where an agent approves, certifies, likes, supports, or sanctions an object. Also called approve, support, certify, sanction. Examples: Liking a post on social media, certifying a product as organic, endorsing a political candidate, giving a positive review.
EndorsementRating: An EndorsementRating is a Rating that expresses a positive level of endorsement, such as a "critic's pick" or a social media "Like," often without a numeric scale. Also called positive rating, approval rating, recommendation. Examples: A "thumbs up" icon, a "recommended by critics" badge, a social media "Like" count, inclusion in a "best of" list.
Energy: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".
EnergyConsumptionDetails: EnergyConsumptionDetails is an Intangible providing information related to the energy efficiency of a product that consumes energy, based on international regulations. Also called energy efficiency data, power usage specifications, consumption metrics. Examples: A product's energy label showing kWh/year, details on standby power consumption, information on energy efficiency class.
EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration: An EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an Enumeration of energy efficiency levels and certifications from various international standards. Also called energy rating, efficiency class, energy certification. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration, EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration.
EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration: An EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration indicating whether a product is EnergyStar certified. Also called Energy Star rating, Energy Star certification. Examples: EnergyStarCertified, NotEnergyStarCertified.
EngineSpecification: An EngineSpecification is a StructuredValue providing details about a vehicle's engine. Also called engine details, motor specs, powertrain information. Examples: Engine type (e.g., V6), displacement (e.g., 2.0L), horsepower, fuel type.
EntertainmentBusiness: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.
EntryPoint: An EntryPoint is an Intangible representing a specific access point within a Web-based protocol. Also called API endpoint, access point, URL entry. Examples: A specific URL for an API call, a login page, a download link, a search form action URL.
Enumeration: An Enumeration is an Intangible representing a list of predefined values or categories. Also called list, category, type. Examples: A list of music genres, a set of clothing sizes, a collection of event statuses.
Episode: An Episode is a CreativeWork representing a single installment of a media series, such as a TV show, radio program, or video game. Also called installment, segment, part. Examples: A single episode of a TV series, a chapter in a podcast, a level in a video game series.
Error: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.
Event: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.
EventAttendanceModeEnumeration: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.
EventReservation: An EventReservation is a Reservation for an event like a concert, sporting event, or lecture. Also called ticket booking, event booking, seat reservation. Examples: A confirmed ticket for a concert, a reservation for a theater play, a booking for a conference session. Distinct from Offer, which describes the availability of tickets for sale.
EventSeries: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.
EventStatusType: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.
EventVenue: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.
ExchangeRateSpecification: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.
ExerciseAction: ExerciseAction is a PlayAction representing the act of participating in exertive activity to improve health and fitness. Also called working out, physical activity, training. Examples: Going for a run, lifting weights, practicing yoga, swimming laps.
ExerciseGym: An ExerciseGym is a SportsActivityLocation that provides facilities for physical exercise. Also called gym, fitness center, health club. Examples: A local fitness gym, a CrossFit box, a university recreation center.
ExercisePlan: An ExercisePlan is a CreativeWork representing a fitness-related activity designed for a specific health purpose, including routines or clinician-prescribed activities. Also called workout plan, fitness regimen, training program. Examples: A 30-day weight loss plan, a physical therapy exercise routine, a marathon training schedule, a yoga sequence.
ExhibitionEvent: An ExhibitionEvent is an Event type focused on displaying items, such as at a museum, library, or tradeshow. Also called exhibit, show, display event. Examples: An art exhibition at a gallery, a historical display at a museum, a trade show for new technologies, a book fair.
FAQPage: A FAQPage is a WebPage presenting one or more frequently asked questions and their answers. Also called Frequently Asked Questions page, Q&A page. Examples: A website's help section with common questions, a product support page listing FAQs, a service's troubleshooting guide.
FMRadioChannel: An FMRadioChannel is a RadioChannel that broadcasts using FM (Frequency Modulation) technology. Also called FM station, FM broadcast channel. Examples: 98.7 FM, a local public radio FM channel, a commercial music FM station.
FastFoodRestaurant: A FastFoodRestaurant is a FoodEstablishment specializing in quickly prepared and served food. Also called quick-service restaurant, drive-thru. Examples: McDonald's, Subway, a local burger joint, a taco stand.
Festival: A Festival is an Event that is a public celebration or series of special events. Also called celebration, gala, fete. Examples: A music festival, a film festival, a cultural heritage festival, a food and wine festival.
FilmAction: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.
FinancialIncentive: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.
FinancialProduct: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.
FinancialService: A FinancialService is a LocalBusiness that provides financial services. Also called bank, credit union, investment firm, insurance company. Examples: A retail bank, a wealth management firm, an insurance agency, a loan provider.
FindAction: FindAction is an Action representing the act of locating an object. Also called discover, locate, unearth. Examples: Finding a lost key, discovering a new species, locating a specific document, unearthing an artifact. Distinct from SearchAction, which is generally a precursor to FindAction.
FireStation: A FireStation is a CivicStructure housing firemen and fire-fighting equipment. Also called fire department, firehouse. Examples: The local city fire station, a volunteer fire department, a regional fire and rescue service.
Flight: A Flight is a Trip representing an airline journey. Also called air travel, plane ride, air route. Examples: Flight BA249 from London to Rio, a domestic flight from New York to Chicago, a charter flight.
FlightReservation: A FlightReservation is a Reservation for air travel. Also called flight booking, airline reservation, plane ticket. Examples: A confirmed booking for a flight, a digital boarding pass, a reservation for a multi-leg journey. Distinct from Offer, which describes the availability of tickets for sale.
Float: Float is a Number data type representing a floating-point number. Also called decimal number, real number. Examples: 3.14, -0.5, 100.0, 2.718.
FloorPlan: A FloorPlan is an Intangible representing an explicit description of a collection of similar accommodations, providing common information like room counts, sizes, and layout diagrams. Also called layout plan, apartment layout, property blueprint. Examples: A floor plan for a two-bedroom apartment, a diagram showing the layout of an office suite, a blueprint for a house model.
Florist: A Florist is a Store that sells flowers and floral arrangements. Also called flower shop, floral designer. Examples: A local flower shop, an online florist delivering bouquets, a wedding floral specialist.
FollowAction: FollowAction is an InteractAction representing the act of forming a unidirectional personal connection with someone or something to receive updates. Also called subscribe, track, observe. Examples: Following a celebrity on social media, subscribing to a news feed, observing a public figure's activities. Distinct from BefriendAction, which implies a reciprocal connection.
FoodEstablishment: A FoodEstablishment is a LocalBusiness primarily involved in food-related services. Also called eatery, restaurant, food service provider. Examples: A restaurant, a cafe, a bakery, a catering company.
FoodEstablishmentReservation: A FoodEstablishmentReservation is a Reservation to dine at a food-related business. Also called restaurant booking, table reservation, dining reservation. Examples: A confirmed table booking at a restaurant, a reservation for a cafe, a booking for a private dining event. Distinct from Offer, which describes the availability of tables for booking.
FoodEvent: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.
FoodService: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.
FulfillmentTypeEnumeration: A FulfillmentTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration representing different ways a product can be fulfilled or delivered. Also called delivery method, order fulfillment type, shipping option. Examples: Delivery, Pickup, InStorePickup, CurbsidePickup.
FundingAgency: A FundingAgency is an Organization that implements FundingSchemes and manages the granting process for projects and activities. Also called grant agency, funding body, research council. Examples: National Institutes of Health (NIH), European Research Council (ERC), Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.
FundingScheme: A FundingScheme is an Organization that defines guidelines, principles, and mechanisms for grant-based funding to support projects and activities. Also called grant program, funding initiative, research funding framework. Examples: EU Horizon 2020, NIH-R01 Grant Program, Wellcome institutional strategic support fund.
FurnitureStore: A FurnitureStore is a Store that sells furniture. Also called home furnishings store, furniture retailer. Examples: IKEA, Ashley Furniture, a local antique furniture shop.
Game: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.
GameAvailabilityEnumeration: A GameAvailabilityEnumeration is an Enumeration indicating the kind of game availability offered for a VideoGame. Also called game access type, availability status. Examples: FullGame, DemoGame, FreeToPlay.
GamePlayMode: A GamePlayMode is an Enumeration indicating whether a game is multi-player, co-op, or single-player. Also called player mode, game type. Examples: SinglePlayer, MultiPlayer, CoOp.
GameServer: A GameServer is an Intangible server that facilitates game interaction in a multiplayer game. Also called game host, multiplayer server. Examples: A dedicated server for an online game, a private game server for friends, a public game server for a large community.
GameServerStatus: A GameServerStatus is a StatusEnumeration representing the operational status of a game server. Also called server status, game server state. Examples: Online, Offline, Maintenance.
GardenStore: A GardenStore is a Store that sells gardening supplies and plants. Also called nursery, garden center, plant shop. Examples: Home Depot Garden Center, a local plant nursery, a specialized seed store.
GasStation: A GasStation is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells fuel for vehicles. Also called petrol station, filling station, service station. Examples: Shell, ExxonMobil, a local independent gas station.
GatedResidenceCommunity: A GatedResidenceCommunity is a Residence type that is a residential area with restricted access. Also called gated community, private estate. Examples: A luxury residential complex with controlled entry, a retirement community with security gates, a private housing development.
GenderType: A GenderType is an Enumeration of genders. Also called sex, gender identity. Examples: Male, Female, NonBinary.
Gene: A Gene is a BioChemEntity representing a discrete unit of inheritance that affects one or more biological traits. Also called genetic unit, hereditary factor. Examples: FOXP2, SCARNA21, the gene for eye color, a specific allele.
GeneralContractor: A GeneralContractor is a HomeAndConstructionBusiness that oversees and manages construction projects. Also called building contractor, construction manager. Examples: A contractor managing a home renovation, a firm overseeing commercial building construction, a project manager for a new development.
GeoCircle: A GeoCircle is a GeoShape representing a circular geographic area, defined by a center point and a radius. Also called circular region, geographic circle. Examples: A 5-mile radius around a city center, a circular search area defined by latitude/longitude and radius, a geofence for a specific location.
GeoCoordinates: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.
GeoShape: A GeoShape is a StructuredValue representing the geographic shape of a place, described using latitude/longitude pairs. Also called geographic area, spatial boundary, region. Examples: A polygon defining a city boundary, a circle representing a search radius, a line segment for a road.
GeospatialGeometry: GeospatialGeometry is an Intangible supertype of GeoShape, designed to accommodate definitions from Geo-Spatial best practices. Also called spatial geometry, geographic feature. Examples: A GeoShape, a KML polygon, a GeoJSON object.
GiveAction: GiveAction is a TransferAction representing the act of transferring ownership of an object to a destination. Also called donate, bestow, grant, hand over. Examples: Giving a gift, donating money to charity, granting a license, handing over a document. Distinct from SendAction, which does not necessarily imply transfer of ownership.
GolfCourse: A GolfCourse is a SportsActivityLocation designed for playing golf. Also called golf club, links. Examples: Augusta National Golf Club, St Andrews Links, a local public golf course.
GovernmentBenefitsType: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.
GovernmentBuilding: A GovernmentBuilding is a civic structure that houses government operations or services. Also called public building, state edifice, official premises. Examples: city hall, parliament building, courthouse, post office. Distinct from GovernmentOffice, which is a specific type of organization within a government building.
GovernmentOffice: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.
GovernmentOrganization: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.
GovernmentPermit: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.
GovernmentService: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.
Grant: A Grant is an intangible, typically financial or quantifiable, allocation of resources from a funder to an organization or person, often supporting specific collective goals or projects. Also called funding award, financial aid, sponsorship, endowment. Examples: research grant, arts grant, student scholarship, disaster relief fund.
GroceryStore: A GroceryStore is a local business that sells food and household supplies. Also called supermarket, food market, grocer. Examples: Whole Foods Market, Safeway, Trader Joe's, local corner store.
Guide: A Guide is a creative work that recommends specific products, services, or aspects of a thing for a user to consider, often detailing features or providing rankings. Also called buying guide, product review, ranked list, how-to manual. Examples: 'Best Laptops of 2023' article, a travel guide to Paris, a car buying guide, a beginner's photography guide. Distinct from HowTo, which provides step-by-step instructions to achieve a result.
HVACBusiness: An HVACBusiness is a home and construction local business specializing in heating, ventilation, and air conditioning services. Also called heating and cooling company, air conditioning service, ventilation contractor. Examples: local AC repair service, furnace installation company, duct cleaning business.
Hackathon: A Hackathon is an event where participants collaboratively engage in intensive computer programming or design over a short period. Also called coding sprint, dev challenge, programming marathon. Examples: university hackathon, corporate innovation sprint, open-source code jam.
HairSalon: A HairSalon is a health and beauty local business offering hair care services. Also called barbershop, beauty parlor, hair studio. Examples: Supercuts, Great Clips, a local independent stylist.
HardwareStore: A HardwareStore is a local business that sells tools, building materials, and home improvement supplies. Also called home improvement store, DIY shop, building supply store. Examples: Home Depot, Lowe's, Ace Hardware, local tool shop.
HealthAndBeautyBusiness: A HealthAndBeautyBusiness is a local business that provides services related to health and personal grooming. Also called wellness business, personal care service, aesthetic clinic. Examples: spa, gym, hair salon, nail salon, massage parlor.
HealthAspectEnumeration: HealthAspectEnumeration is an enumeration of various aspects of health content, used to describe specific facets of health topics online. Also called health content categories, medical information facets, wellness topic types. Examples: 'Symptoms', 'Treatments', 'Causes', 'Prevention'.
HealthClub: A HealthClub is a health and beauty local business providing facilities and services for physical fitness and wellness. Also called gym, fitness center, wellness club, athletic club. Examples: Gold's Gym, Planet Fitness, YMCA, a local yoga studio.
HealthInsurancePlan: A HealthInsurancePlan is an intangible financial product that specifies coverage and costs for medical services, such as PPOs, EPOs, and HMOs. Also called medical insurance policy, healthcare plan, health coverage. Examples: Blue Cross PPO, Kaiser Permanente HMO, Medicare Advantage plan. Distinct from HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification, which describes patient costs under a plan, and HealthPlanFormulary, which details drug coverage.
HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification: A HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification is an intangible description of the patient's financial responsibilities, such as deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance, under a specific health insurance plan. Also called patient cost details, insurance out-of-pocket, healthcare expense breakdown. Examples: a document detailing a plan's deductible, copay for specialist visits, coinsurance percentage. Distinct from HealthInsurancePlan, which is the overall policy, and HealthPlanFormulary, which focuses specifically on prescription drug costs.
HealthPlanFormulary: A HealthPlanFormulary is an intangible specification for the costs and coverage of prescription drugs under a given health insurance plan. Also called drug list, prescription drug coverage, medication formulary. Examples: a list of covered medications, a tiered drug pricing schedule, a preferred drug list. Distinct from HealthInsurancePlan, which is the overall policy, and HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification, which covers general patient costs beyond just drugs.
HealthPlanNetwork: A HealthPlanNetwork is an intangible collection of healthcare providers, such as doctors and hospitals, that contract with a health insurance plan to provide services at negotiated rates. Also called provider network, insurance network, healthcare provider group. Examples: an HMO network, a PPO network, a specific hospital system affiliated with an insurer.
HealthTopicContent: HealthTopicContent is web content about a specific aspect of a health topic, such as a medical condition, its symptoms, or treatments. Also called medical web content, health information article, wellness resource. Examples: an article explaining diabetes symptoms, a webpage detailing cancer treatments, a video on heart disease prevention.
HighSchool: A HighSchool is an educational organization and civic structure providing secondary education. Also called secondary school, senior high, academy. Examples: Springfield High School, Northwood Academy, a local public high school.
HinduTemple: A HinduTemple is a place of worship and civic structure dedicated to Hindu deities. Also called Mandir, Hindu shrine, temple. Examples: Akshardham Temple, Sri Venkateswara Temple, a local Hindu community temple.
HobbyShop: A HobbyShop is a local business that sells materials and supplies for various hobbies. Also called craft store, model shop, specialty hobby retailer. Examples: a model train store, an art supply shop, a gaming store, a fabric and yarn store.
HomeAndConstructionBusiness: A HomeAndConstructionBusiness is a local business that provides services related to homes and buildings, such as construction, repair, or maintenance. Also called building contractor, home services company, construction firm. Examples: a general contractor, a plumbing service, a roofing company, a landscaping business.
HomeGoodsStore: A HomeGoodsStore is a local business that sells items for furnishing and decorating a home. Also called home decor store, furniture shop, housewares retailer. Examples: IKEA, Pottery Barn, Bed Bath & Beyond, a local kitchenware store.
Hospital: A Hospital is a civic structure and medical institution providing patient treatment with specialized medical and nursing staff and equipment. Also called medical center, clinic, healthcare facility. Examples: Mayo Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital, a local emergency room.
Hostel: A Hostel is a lodging business offering inexpensive accommodation, often featuring shared dormitories and communal facilities. Also called youth hostel, budget accommodation, backpacker's lodge. Examples: Generator Hostel, a local backpacker hostel, a mountain hut. Distinct from Hotel, which typically offers private rooms and more extensive services.
Hotel: A Hotel is a lodging business providing short-term, paid accommodation, typically in private rooms. Also called inn, motel, lodging establishment. Examples: Hilton Hotel, Marriott International, a boutique hotel. Distinct from Hostel, which often provides cheaper, shared dormitory-style accommodation.
HotelRoom: A HotelRoom is a specific accommodation unit within a hotel. Also called guest room, hotel suite, lodging unit. Examples: a standard double room, a king suite, a connecting room. Distinct from Room, which is a general type of accommodation that could be in any building.
House: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.
HousePainter: A HousePainter is a home and construction local business providing painting services for houses and other structures. Also called painting contractor, residential painter, decorator. Examples: a local exterior painting service, an interior decorator, a commercial painting company.
HowTo: A HowTo is a creative work providing instructions that explain how to achieve a specific result through a sequence of steps. Also called instruction manual, tutorial, guide, DIY guide. Examples: a recipe for baking a cake, instructions for assembling furniture, a guide on changing a car tire. Distinct from Guide, which recommends products or aspects to consider, rather than providing step-by-step actions.
HowToDirection: A HowToDirection is a creative work representing a single action or instruction within a HowTo guide. Also called instruction step, action item, procedural command. Examples: 'Mix ingredients thoroughly,' 'Turn the knob clockwise,' 'Press the power button.' Distinct from HowToTip, which provides supplementary information rather than a direct action.
HowToItem: A HowToItem is a list item used as either a tool or supply when following instructions in a HowTo guide. Also called instruction component, how-to resource, procedural element. Examples: a screwdriver, flour, a measuring cup, a specific software application.
HowToSection: A HowToSection is a creative work representing a sub-grouping of steps within a larger HowTo guide. Also called instruction chapter, procedural segment, how-to module. Examples: 'Preparing the Dough' in a bread recipe, 'Connecting the Wires' in an electronics manual.
HowToStep: A HowToStep is a creative work representing an ordered step in a HowTo guide, which can contain directions and/or tips. Also called instruction stage, procedural step, action sequence. Examples: 'Step 1: Gather Ingredients,' 'Step 2: Preheat Oven,' 'Step 3: Bake for 30 minutes.'
HowToSupply: A HowToSupply is a HowToItem that is consumed or used up when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. Also called consumable item, ingredient, material. Examples: flour, sugar, paint, batteries. Distinct from HowToTool, which is used but not consumed.
HowToTip: A HowToTip is a creative work providing supplementary information or advice within a HowTo guide, rather than a direct action. Also called instruction hint, helpful advice, procedural note. Examples: 'Tip: Use fresh ingredients for best results,' 'Warning: Do not overtighten,' 'Pro-tip: Chill the dough for an hour.' Distinct from HowToDirection, which specifies a direct action to perform.
HowToTool: A HowToTool is a HowToItem that is used but not consumed when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. Also called instrument, utensil, equipment. Examples: a screwdriver, a mixing bowl, a hammer, a computer. Distinct from HowToSupply, which is consumed during the process.
HyperToc: A HyperToc is a creative work representing a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects like videos or audio, with entries indicating specific sections. Also called interactive table of contents, media chapter list, navigable index. Examples: a chapter list for a long documentary video, an interactive index for an audio lecture series.
HyperTocEntry: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.
IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration: IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration is a media enumeration of IPTC 'Digital Source' codes, providing information about the origin of a digital media object. Also called digital media source types, IPTC source codes, content origin categories. Examples: 'Original', 'Scanned Print', 'Digital Capture', 'Composite'.
ITNonprofitType: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.
IceCreamShop: An IceCreamShop is a food establishment local business specializing in selling ice cream and related frozen desserts. Also called gelateria, ice cream parlor, frozen dessert shop. Examples: Baskin-Robbins, Ben & Jerry's Scoop Shop, a local artisanal ice cream store.
IgnoreAction: An IgnoreAction is an assess action representing the act of intentionally disregarding an object. Also called disregard action, overlook action, dismiss action. Examples: ignoring a spam email, dismissing a notification, overlooking a minor error. Distinct from DeleteAction, which removes an object, and RejectAction, which refuses an offer or proposal.
ImageGallery: An ImageGallery is a collection page web page type specifically designed to display a collection of images. Also called photo gallery, picture album, visual collection page. Examples: a wedding photo gallery, a portfolio of landscape images, a product image carousel. Distinct from VideoGallery, which displays videos, and MediaGallery, which is a more general type.
ImageObject: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.
ImageObjectSnapshot: An ImageObjectSnapshot is a specific, byte-for-byte identical version of an ImageObject, where identity is determined by the exact content including embedded metadata. Also called exact image copy, immutable image, content-identical image. Examples: a specific version of a digital photograph with its original EXIF data, a cryptographically hashed image file. Distinct from ImageObject, which is the general concept of an image file, not necessarily a specific, immutable version.
ImagingTest: An ImagingTest is a medical test that uses any medical imaging modality for diagnostic purposes. Also called medical scan, diagnostic imaging, radiology test. Examples: X-ray, MRI scan, CT scan, ultrasound. Distinct from BloodTest, which analyzes blood samples, and PathologyTest, which examines tissues.
IncentiveQualifiedExpenseType: IncentiveQualifiedExpenseType is an enumeration of the types of expenses that are covered by a financial incentive. Also called eligible expense categories, incentive coverage types, qualified cost types. Examples: 'Goods', 'Services', 'Labor', 'Materials'.
IncentiveStatus: IncentiveStatus is an enumeration describing the current status of an incentive, such as whether it is active or expired. Also called incentive state, benefit status, program condition. Examples: 'Active', 'Expired', 'Pending', 'Suspended'.
IncentiveType: IncentiveType is an enumeration of common financial incentives for products, including tax credits, rebates, and subsidies. Also called financial benefit type, stimulus category, grant type. Examples: 'TaxCredit', 'Rebate', 'Subsidy', 'TaxDeduction'.
IndividualPhysician: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.
IndividualProduct: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.
InfectiousAgentClass: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.
InfectiousDisease: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.
InformAction: An InformAction is a communicate action representing the act of notifying someone of pertinent information without expecting a response. Also called notify action, announce action, advise action. Examples: sending a broadcast email, posting a public announcement, informing a colleague about a meeting change. Distinct from AskAction, which seeks information, and ReplyAction, which responds to communication.
InsertAction: An InsertAction is an add action representing the act of adding an object at a specific location within an ordered collection. Also called place action, embed action, inject action. Examples: inserting a new paragraph into a document, adding an item to a shopping cart, placing a card into a deck. Distinct from AddAction, which is a more general act of adding without specifying location.
InstallAction: An InstallAction is a consume action representing the act of installing an application or software. Also called set up action, deploy action, load software. Examples: installing a new app on a phone, setting up an operating system, deploying a server application.
InstantaneousEvent: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.
InsuranceAgency: An InsuranceAgency is a financial service local business that provides insurance-related services. Also called insurance broker, insurance provider, insurance firm. Examples: State Farm, Geico, a local independent insurance agent.
Intangible: Intangible is a utility class serving as an umbrella for things that lack physical form, such as quantities, structured values, and concepts. Also called abstract entity, non-physical item, conceptual object. Examples: a number, a permit, a service, a list. Distinct from Thing, which is the root of all types, and CreativeWork, which is a specific type of intangible.
Integer: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.
InteractAction: An InteractAction is an action representing the act of interacting with another person or organization. Also called engagement action, social action, communication action. Examples: communicating, joining, inviting, following. Distinct from CommunicateAction, which is a specific type of interaction focused on information exchange.
InteractionCounter: An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker. Examples: number of likes, view count, comment count, share count.
InternetCafe: An InternetCafe is a local business providing public access to computers with internet connectivity, often alongside food and beverages. Also called cyber cafe, web cafe, net cafe. Examples: a local internet cafe, a gaming cafe with internet access.
InvestmentFund: An InvestmentFund is a financial product service that pools capital from multiple investors to reinvest into various assets like stocks and bonds. Also called mutual fund, hedge fund, pooled investment vehicle. Examples: Vanguard S&P 500 Index Fund, a private equity fund, a real estate investment trust (REIT). Distinct from InvestmentOrDeposit, which is a broader category for financial products requiring fund transfers for potential returns.
InvestmentOrDeposit: An InvestmentOrDeposit is a financial product service that typically requires a client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial returns. Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement. Examples: a savings account, a certificate of deposit (CD), a stock market investment. Distinct from InvestmentFund, which is a specific type of pooled investment, and LoanOrCredit, which involves borrowing.
InviteAction: An InviteAction is a communicate action representing the act of asking someone to attend an event. Also called invitation action, request attendance, solicit presence. Examples: sending a party invitation, inviting a speaker to a conference, asking a friend to dinner. Distinct from RsvpAction, which is the reciprocal act of responding to an invitation.
Invoice: An Invoice is an intangible statement detailing the money due for goods or services; a bill. Also called bill, statement of account, charge slip. Examples: a utility bill, a contractor's invoice for services, a restaurant check.
ItemAvailability: ItemAvailability is an enumeration of possible product availability options. Also called product status, stock status, inventory condition. Examples: 'InStock', 'OutOfStock', 'PreOrder', 'InStoreOnly'.
ItemList: An ItemList is an intangible collection of items of any sort, often ordered or ranked. Also called list, collection, sequence, array. Examples: 'Top 10 Movies,' a shopping list, a playlist, a table of contents. Distinct from ListItem, which is a single entry within an ItemList.
ItemListOrderType: ItemListOrderType is an enumeration for values indicating how an ordered ItemList is organized. Also called list sorting type, item sequence order, collection arrangement. Examples: 'Ascending', 'Descending', 'Unordered'.
ItemPage: An ItemPage is a web page devoted to a single item, such as a particular product or hotel. Also called product page, detail page, single item view. Examples: an Amazon product page, a hotel booking page for a specific hotel, a blog post about one topic. Distinct from CollectionPage, which displays multiple items.
JewelryStore: A JewelryStore is a local business that sells jewelry. Also called jeweler, gem shop, watch store. Examples: Tiffany & Co., Pandora, a local independent jeweler.
JobPosting: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.
JoinAction: A JoinAction is an interact action where an agent becomes part of an event or group with other participants. Also called participate action, become member, attend action. Examples: joining a club, attending a meeting, becoming a member of a team. Distinct from RegisterAction, which is signing up for a service, and SubscribeAction, which implies receiving updates.
Joint: A Joint is an anatomical structure where two or more bones make contact, facilitating movement or providing stability. Also called articulation, bone joint, anatomical junction. Examples: knee joint, elbow joint, hip joint, shoulder joint. Distinct from Bone, which is a single skeletal component.
LakeBodyOfWater: A LakeBodyOfWater is a landform representing a large body of still water surrounded by land. Also called lake, inland sea, reservoir. Examples: Lake Superior, Lake Tahoe, Lake Pontchartrain. Distinct from River, which is flowing water, and OceanBodyOfWater, which is a large saltwater body.
Landform: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.
LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.
Language: Language is an intangible representing natural languages such as Spanish or English, distinct from programming languages. Also called natural tongue, human language, spoken language. Examples: English, Spanish, Mandarin, Arabic. Distinct from ComputerLanguage, which refers to programming languages.
LearningResource: A LearningResource is a creative work explicitly oriented towards learning, education, or skill acquisition. Also called educational material, study resource, instructional content. Examples: a textbook, an online course module, a tutorial video, a practice worksheet. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.
LeaveAction: A LeaveAction is an interact action where an agent departs from an event or group. Also called depart action, exit action, withdraw action. Examples: leaving a meeting, exiting a social group, departing from a party. Distinct from JoinAction, which is its antonym, and UnRegisterAction, which implies unsubscribing from a service.
LegalForceStatus: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.
LegalService: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.
LegalValueLevel: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.
Legislation: Legislation is a creative work representing a legal document such as an act, decree, or bill, or a component thereof. Also called law, statute, legal act, regulation. Examples: the Civil Rights Act, a local ordinance, a proposed bill in parliament. Distinct from LegislationObject, which is a specific file containing the legislation.
LegislationObject: A LegislationObject is a specific file or object containing a Legislation, which can exist in multiple formats. Also called legal document file, legislation artifact, law document. Examples: a PDF of a specific law, an HTML version of a regulation, a digitally signed legal document. Distinct from Legislation, which is the abstract legal document itself.
LegislativeBuilding: A LegislativeBuilding is a government building civic structure where legislative bodies meet and conduct their work. Also called capitol building, parliament house, assembly hall. Examples: the U.S. Capitol, a state capitol building, the Houses of Parliament. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.
LendAction: A LendAction is a transfer action representing the act of providing an object under an agreement that it will be returned later. Also called loan action, provide temporarily, furnish on credit. Examples: lending a book to a friend, loaning money, renting out equipment. Distinct from BorrowAction, which is the reciprocal act of receiving an object with the intent to return it.
Library: A Library is a local business that provides access to books, media, and information resources. Also called public library, academic library, media center. Examples: New York Public Library, a university library, a local community library. Distinct from LibrarySystem, which is a collaborative network of libraries.
LibrarySystem: A LibrarySystem is an organization representing a collaborative network or system among several libraries. Also called library consortium, library network, regional library system. Examples: a state library system, a university library consortium, a public library district. Distinct from Library, which is a single physical or organizational entity.
LifestyleModification: A LifestyleModification is a medical entity representing a process of care involving changes to diet, exercise, and other habits to improve a health condition. Also called health habit change, wellness intervention, behavioral therapy. Examples: a weight loss program, a smoking cessation plan, a stress reduction regimen.
Ligament: A Ligament is an anatomical structure medical entity consisting of tough, fibrous connective tissue that connects bones and supports joints. Also called connective tissue band, joint stabilizer, fibrous band. Examples: anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), medial collateral ligament (MCL), ankle ligaments. Distinct from Tendon, which connects muscle to bone.
LikeAction: A LikeAction is a react action representing the act of expressing a positive sentiment about an object. Also called approve action, endorse action, favorite action. Examples: liking a post on social media, giving a thumbs-up to a video, expressing approval for an idea. Distinct from DislikeAction, which expresses negative sentiment.
LinkRole: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.
LiquorStore: A LiquorStore is a local business that sells alcoholic beverages such as wine, beer, and spirits. Also called off-license, bottle shop, wine shop, spirits retailer. Examples: a local wine and spirits shop, a beer distributor, a duty-free liquor store.
ListItem: A ListItem is an intangible representing a single entry within a list, such as a step in a checklist or a how-to description. Also called list entry, item in a sequence, element of a list. Examples: 'Buy milk,' 'Step 1: Preheat oven,' 'First item.' Distinct from ItemList, which is the collection of items.
ListenAction: The act of consuming audio content, as a type of action. Also called hearing, audio consumption, listening activity. Examples: listening to music, hearing a podcast, attending an audio lecture.
LiteraryEvent: An event focused on literature, such as readings, book launches, or discussions. Also called book event, author appearance, literary gathering. Examples: a poetry reading, a book signing, a literary festival, a panel discussion with authors.
LiveBlogPosting: A blog post that provides continuous, real-time textual coverage of an ongoing event. Also called live blog, real-time blog, event coverage blog. Examples: a live blog of a sports game, a live blog of a political debate, a live blog of a breaking news event. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a general blog post without the real-time, continuous update focus.
LoanOrCredit: A financial product representing an amount of money loaned or a line of credit offered under specific terms and charges. Also called credit facility, lending product, financial loan. Examples: a personal loan, a credit card, a mortgage, a business line of credit. Distinct from MortgageLoan, which is specifically a loan secured by real estate.
LocalBusiness: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.
LocationFeatureSpecification: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".
Locksmith: A local business specializing in locks and keys. Also called key maker, lock specialist, security technician. Examples: "ABC Locksmiths", "24/7 Emergency Locksmith", "City Lock & Key".
LodgingBusiness: A local business that provides temporary accommodation for travelers or guests. Also called accommodation provider, hospitality business, hotelier. Examples: a hotel, a motel, an inn, a bed and breakfast, a resort. Distinct from Hotel, which is a specific type of lodging business.
LodgingReservation: A reservation for temporary accommodation at a lodging business like a hotel, motel, or inn. Also called hotel booking, accommodation booking, room reservation. Examples: a confirmed hotel room booking, a motel reservation confirmation, an inn booking. Distinct from Reservation, which is a general booking for any service or item.
LoginAction: The action of gaining access to a device or application by providing credentials. Also called sign in, log on, user authentication. Examples: logging into a website, signing into a mobile app, logging onto a computer. Distinct from ControlAction, which is a broader category for actions that control something.
LoseAction: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.
LymphaticVessel: A type of vessel within the anatomical structure of the body that specifically carries lymph fluid towards the heart. Also called lymph vessel, lymphatic duct, lymphangion. Examples: thoracic duct, right lymphatic duct, lacteal. Distinct from BloodVessel, which carries blood.
Manuscript: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.
Map: A creative work that visually represents an area, showing features like roads, cities, or terrain. Also called cartographic representation, geographical chart, atlas page. Examples: a road map, a topographic map, a subway map, a world atlas.
MapCategoryType: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".
MarryAction: The act of entering into marriage with another person. Also called get married, wed, tie the knot. Examples: a wedding ceremony, a civil marriage, eloping.
Mass: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.
MathSolver: A creative work that is a tool or application capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems. Also called mathematical calculator, problem solver, equation solver. Examples: an online algebra solver, a geometry calculator, a calculus problem-solving app.
MaximumDoseSchedule: A medical dose schedule specifying the highest recommended safe dosage for a drug or supplement, as advised by an authority or manufacturer. Also called max dosage, upper dose limit, safe dose ceiling. Examples: "maximum 2 tablets per day", "not to exceed 100mg daily", "maximum single dose 500mg".
MeasurementMethodEnum: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".
MeasurementTypeEnumeration: An enumeration of common types or dimensions of measurements. Also called dimension type, measurement category, sizing parameter. Examples: "chest circumference", "inseam length", "screw gauge", "wheel diameter".
MediaEnumeration: An enumeration providing codes and labels useful for describing media objects. Also called media classification, media type list, content category. Examples: "Video", "Audio", "Image", "Text".
MediaGallery: A web page that serves as a collection page for various media, such as images, videos, and other multimedia. Also called multimedia gallery, photo and video collection, digital media showcase. Examples: a website's image gallery, a video portfolio page, a mixed-media art exhibition page.
MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration: An enumeration of codes used to indicate the authenticity of a media object in the context of its publication or sharing, especially regarding manipulation. Also called media authenticity rating, manipulation type, content integrity code. Examples: "original media", "transformed media", "edited media", "staged media", "misleading context".
MediaObject: A creative work representing a media object like an image, video, audio, or text, which can be embedded or downloaded. Also called digital media asset, multimedia file, content object. Examples: a JPEG image file, an MP4 video, an MP3 audio track, a PDF document. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.
MediaReview: A specialized review dedicated to evaluating online media content, often in the context of fact-checking and misinformation. Also called media fact-check, content authenticity review, misinformation analysis. Examples: a fact-check of a viral video, an analysis of a manipulated image, a review of a misleading news article. Distinct from Review, which is a general evaluation of any item or service.
MediaReviewItem: A creative work representing an item or group of items treated as a single unit for evaluation within a MediaReview. Also called reviewed media unit, content item for review, media subject. Examples: a specific viral video, a collection of related images, a particular news clip.
MediaSubscription: An intangible service that grants a user access to media content, including audio, video, or books. Also called content subscription, media access plan, digital media membership. Examples: a streaming video subscription, an audiobook service membership, a digital newspaper subscription.
MedicalAudience: An audience type representing target groups for medical web pages. Also called healthcare audience, patient demographic, medical readership. Examples: "patients", "healthcare professionals", "medical researchers", "general public interested in health".
MedicalAudienceType: An enumeration of specific target audience types for medical web pages. Also called medical audience category, healthcare target group, patient type. Examples: "Patient", "Physician", "Researcher", "Caregiver".
MedicalBusiness: A local business operating for medical purposes, which can be physical or virtual. Also called healthcare business, medical practice, health services provider. Examples: a dental office, a physical therapy clinic, a telemedicine service, a diagnostic lab. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which is a broader category for any local business.
MedicalCause: A medical entity representing the causative agent(s) responsible for a pathophysiologic process leading to a medical condition, symptom, or sign. Also called etiology, causative factor, underlying reason. Examples: "HIV virus" as a cause of AIDS, "pulmonary embolism" as a cause of cardiac arrest, "bacterial infection".
MedicalClinic: A medical business facility, often associated with a hospital, dedicated to specific diagnosis and/or healthcare, typically for outpatients but sometimes inpatients. Also called clinic, healthcare center, medical facility. Examples: a dermatology clinic, a walk-in clinic, a university health clinic, a family practice. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger institution providing comprehensive medical care.
MedicalCode: A category code representing a standardized code for a medical entity. Also called medical identifier, health code, clinical code. Examples: "ICD-10 code", "SNOMED CT code", "CPT code", "RxNorm identifier".
MedicalCondition: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".
MedicalConditionStage: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".
MedicalContraindication: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a particular medical therapy. Also called contraindication, medical warning, therapy restriction. Examples: "pregnancy" for certain medications, "allergy to penicillin", "severe kidney disease".
MedicalDevice: A medical entity representing any object used in a medical capacity for diagnosing or treating a patient. Also called medical instrument, healthcare apparatus, diagnostic tool. Examples: a stethoscope, an MRI machine, a surgical scalpel, a blood pressure monitor.
MedicalDevicePurpose: An enumeration of categories for medical devices, organized by their purpose or intended use. Also called device use, medical equipment function, intended purpose. Examples: "Diagnostic", "Therapeutic", "Surgical", "Monitoring".
MedicalEntity: The most generic type of entity related to health and the practice of medicine. Also called healthcare entity, medical concept, health-related item. Examples: a disease, a drug, a doctor, a medical procedure, a hospital. Distinct from Thing, which is the root of all schema.org types.
MedicalEnumeration: An enumeration related to health and the practice of medicine, used to attribute qualities or list elements in medical contexts. Also called medical list, healthcare category, clinical classification. Examples: "MedicalSpecialty", "MedicalImagingTechnique", "MedicalStudyStatus". Distinct from Enumeration, which is a broader category for any list of items.
MedicalEvidenceLevel: An enumeration representing the level of evidence supporting a medical guideline. Also called evidence strength, guideline reliability, data quality level. Examples: "Level A evidence", "Grade 1 recommendation", "strong evidence".
MedicalGuideline: A medical entity representing a recommendation made by a standard society or consensus statement on how to diagnose and treat a particular condition. Also called clinical guideline, practice recommendation, medical protocol. Examples: "AHA/ACC Heart Failure Guideline", "NICE guidelines for diabetes management", "WHO recommendations for vaccination".
MedicalGuidelineContraindication: A medical guideline that specifically designates a process as harmful, supported by sound data. Also called contraindicated guideline, harmful practice warning, medical prohibition. Examples: "guideline against routine antibiotic use for viral infections", "contraindication for specific surgical techniques". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineRecommendation, which suggests an efficacious process.
MedicalGuidelineRecommendation: A medical guideline that recommends a process as efficacious, supported by sound data. Also called recommended guideline, best practice recommendation, medical advice. Examples: "guideline recommending statins for high cholesterol", "recommendation for early cancer screening". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineContraindication, which warns against a harmful process.
MedicalImagingTechnique: An enumeration of medical imaging modalities typically used for diagnostic purposes. Also called imaging method, diagnostic scan type, radiology technique. Examples: "MRI", "CT scan", "X-ray", "Ultrasound", "PET scan".
MedicalIndication: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that suggests the use of a medical therapy. Also called indication for treatment, therapeutic rationale, medical justification. Examples: "high blood pressure" as an indication for antihypertensive drugs, "fever" as an indication for antipyretics.
MedicalIntangible: A utility class under MedicalEntity for various intangible concepts in the medical space. Also called medical abstract, healthcare concept, clinical intangible. Examples: "MedicalConditionStage", "DoseSchedule", "MedicalCode". Distinct from MedicalEntity, which is the broader category for all medical things.
MedicalObservationalStudy: A medical study that infers the effect of a treatment by observing a cohort of subjects over time, without investigator control over treatment assignment. Also called observational research, cohort study, epidemiological study. Examples: a study tracking health outcomes in smokers vs. non-smokers, a study on diet and disease incidence. Distinct from MedicalTrial, where subjects are randomly assigned to treatment groups.
MedicalObservationalStudyDesign: An enumeration of design models for observational medical studies. Also called observational study type, research design, epidemiological design. Examples: "CohortStudy", "CaseControlStudy", "CrossSectionalStudy".
MedicalOrganization: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.
MedicalProcedure: A medical entity representing a process of care, invasive or non-invasive, used for diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, or palliative purposes. Also called medical intervention, clinical procedure, healthcare process. Examples: "surgery", "biopsy", "vaccination", "physical therapy".
MedicalProcedureType: An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures. Also called procedure category, intervention type, clinical technique. Examples: "DiagnosticProcedure", "TherapeuticProcedure", "SurgicalProcedure".
MedicalRiskCalculator: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.
MedicalRiskEstimator: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.
MedicalRiskFactor: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.
MedicalRiskScore: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.
MedicalScholarlyArticle: A scholarly article specifically within the medical domain. Also called medical journal article, clinical research paper, healthcare publication. Examples: a peer-reviewed article on a new drug, a research paper on surgical techniques, a review article on a disease. Distinct from ScholarlyArticle, which is a broader category for academic papers.
MedicalSign: A medical sign or symptom that is an objective physical manifestation of a medical condition, discoverable by diagnostic tests or physical examination. Also called objective symptom, clinical sign, diagnostic finding. Examples: "fever", "rash", "high blood pressure", "swelling". Distinct from MedicalSymptom, which is subjective and reported by the patient.
MedicalSignOrSymptom: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.
MedicalSpecialty: An enumeration representing any specific branch of medical science or practice, including clinical and allied health specialties. Also called medical field, clinical discipline, healthcare area. Examples: "Cardiology", "Pediatrics", "Oncology", "Physical Therapy", "Dentistry".
MedicalStudy: A medical entity that is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health. Also called clinical study, health research, medical investigation. Examples: a drug trial, an epidemiological survey, a patient registry. Distinct from MedicalScholarlyArticle, which is the publication of study results, not the study itself.
MedicalStudyStatus: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".
MedicalSymptom: A medical sign or symptom that is a subjective complaint sensed and expressed by the patient. Also called subjective symptom, patient complaint, reported feeling. Examples: "stomachache", "lower-back pain", "fatigue", "headache", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalSign, which is an objective finding.
MedicalTest: A medical entity representing any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes. Also called diagnostic test, clinical examination, medical screening. Examples: "blood test", "urine test", "MRI scan", "biopsy", "physical exam".
MedicalTestPanel: A medical test that is a collection of tests commonly ordered together. Also called test battery, diagnostic panel, group of tests. Examples: "complete blood count (CBC)", "liver function panel", "metabolic panel". Distinct from MedicalTest, which can be a single test.
MedicalTherapy: A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen. Examples: "pharmacotherapy", "behavioral therapy", "supportive therapy", "dialysis". Distinct from MedicalProcedure, which is a broader category including diagnostic procedures.
MedicalTrial: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.
MedicalTrialDesign: An enumeration of design models for medical trials. Also called clinical trial design, trial methodology, study architecture. Examples: "RandomizedControlledTrial", "SingleBlindTrial", "DoubleBlindTrial", "CrossoverTrial".
MedicalWebPage: A web page that specifically provides medical information. Also called health information page, clinical webpage, medical content page. Examples: a page describing a disease, a page explaining a medical procedure, a doctor's profile page. Distinct from WebPage, which is a broader category for any web document.
MedicineSystem: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".
MeetingRoom: A room within an accommodation, such as a hotel, provided for singular events like business conferences and meetings. Also called conference room, conference hall, boardroom, event space. Examples: a hotel's grand ballroom, a corporate meeting room, a small seminar room. Distinct from Room, which is a general category for any room.
MemberProgram: An intangible loyalty or membership program that offers specific benefits to its members. Also called loyalty program, membership scheme, rewards program. Examples: an airline frequent flyer program, a supermarket loyalty card, a gym membership.
MemberProgramTier: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".
MensClothingStore: A local business that is a store specializing in men's clothing. Also called men's apparel shop, menswear store, gentlemen's outfitter. Examples: "Brooks Brothers", "Men's Wearhouse", a local boutique for men. Distinct from ClothingStore, which is a broader category.
Menu: A creative work that is a structured representation of food or drink items available from a food establishment. Also called restaurant menu, food list, beverage list. Examples: a dinner menu, a wine list, a dessert menu, a cafe menu.
