Series: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.
Service: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.
ServiceChannel: A specific means or method for accessing a service, such as a website, phone number, or physical office. Also called access point, service delivery method, contact channel, customer touchpoint. Examples: a company's customer service hotline, an online booking portal, a government agency's physical office, a mobile app.
ServicePeriod: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.
ShareAction: The act of distributing content to others for their amusement or edification. Also called distributing, posting, circulating, spreading. Examples: sharing a news article on social media, forwarding an email, posting a photo to a group chat.
SheetMusic: Printed or written musical notation, as distinct from a performance or recording. Also called musical score, notation, music manuscript, song sheet. Examples: a piano concerto score, guitar tablature, a vocal sheet for a song, an orchestral score.
ShippingConditions: A structured value describing constraints and information about how a product can be shipped, potentially applying to specific product attributes. Also called shipping rules, delivery terms, freight conditions, shipping policy. Examples: free shipping for orders over $50, express shipping for lightweight items, international shipping restrictions.
ShippingDeliveryTime: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.
ShippingRateSettings: A structured value representing reusable shipping rate information, often linked to an offer via a shipping settings link. Also called shipping cost rules, freight pricing, delivery charges configuration. Examples: a flat rate shipping setting for standard delivery, a weight-based shipping rate table, a zone-based shipping cost.
ShippingService: A structured value defining the criteria used to determine if and how an offer can be shipped to a customer. Also called delivery option, shipping method, freight service, courier choice. Examples: 'Standard Ground Shipping', 'Expedited Air Delivery', 'International Economy Shipping'.
ShoeStore: A retail store specializing in the sale of footwear. Also called footwear shop, shoe retailer, boot store. Examples: 'Foot Locker', 'DSW Designer Shoe Warehouse', 'Local Shoe Boutique'.
ShoppingCenter: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.
ShortStory: A brief work of literature, typically written in narrative prose, focusing on a single plot or theme. Also called tale, novelette, short fiction, narrative. Examples: Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Tell-Tale Heart', O. Henry's 'The Gift of the Magi', a story from a literary magazine.
SingleFamilyResidence: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.
SiteNavigationElement: A web page element that provides navigation links or controls for a website. Also called navigation menu, website menu, nav bar, site map. Examples: the main menu bar at the top of a website, a sidebar navigation, a footer navigation.
SizeGroupEnumeration: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.
SizeSpecification: Properties related to a product's size, including a size code, system, group, and measurements. Also called product dimensions, sizing details, garment measurements, fit specifications. Examples: a shirt with size 'M' (Medium) in 'US' size system, a shoe with 'EU 42' size, a dress with 'Petite' size group.
SizeSystemEnumeration: An enumeration of common size systems used for different product categories. Also called sizing standard, measurement system, apparel sizing convention. Examples: 'US', 'UK', 'EU', 'EN-13402', 'Imperial'.
SkiResort: A lodging business and recreational area specifically designed for skiing and other winter sports. Also called ski area, winter resort, mountain resort. Examples: 'Aspen Snowmass', 'Whistler Blackcomb', 'Courchevel'.
SocialEvent: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.
SocialMediaPosting: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.
SoftwareApplication: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.
SoftwareSourceCode: The human-readable instructions written in a programming language that define a software application. Also called source code, program code, script, code snippet. Examples: Python script for data analysis, C++ code for a game engine, HTML/CSS/JavaScript for a website, a Java class file.
SolveMathAction: The action of taking a mathematical expression and directing users to a resource capable of solving or simplifying it. Also called math solving, equation solving, calculation action. Examples: entering '2+2' into a calculator app, inputting a complex equation into Wolfram Alpha, using a math solver website.
SomeProducts: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.
SpeakableSpecification: A specification indicating, typically via CSS selectors or XPath, which sections of a document are particularly suitable for text-to-speech conversion. Also called speakable content definition, text-to-speech markup, voice-friendly section. Examples: a specification highlighting the main article text on a news page, a definition for a recipe's ingredients list.
SpecialAnnouncement: A date-stamped textual information update from a locally-oriented organization, often related to urgent crisis situations, including contextual web links and structured data. Also called public notice, crisis update, community alert, emergency announcement. Examples: a school closure announcement due to weather, a pharmacy's updated operating hours during a pandemic, a local government's public health advisory.
Specialty: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.
SportingGoodsStore: A retail store specializing in the sale of equipment and apparel for sports and outdoor activities. Also called sports shop, athletic store, outdoor gear retailer. Examples: 'Dick's Sporting Goods', 'REI', 'Decathlon'.
SportsActivityLocation: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.
SportsClub: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.
SportsEvent: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.
SportsOrganization: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.
SportsTeam: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.
SpreadsheetDigitalDocument: A digital document designed for organizing and analyzing data in rows and columns, typically containing formulas and charts. Also called spreadsheet file, data sheet, workbook, Excel file. Examples: a budget spreadsheet, a sales report in Google Sheets, a financial model in Microsoft Excel.
StadiumOrArena: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.
State: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.
Statement: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.
StatisticalPopulation: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.
StatisticalVariable: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.
StatusEnumeration: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.
SteeringPositionValue: A value indicating the steering position of a vehicle. Also called steering side, driver's side, vehicle control position. Examples: 'LeftHandDriving', 'RightHandDriving'.
Store: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.
StructuredValue: A value for a property that has a complex internal structure rather than being a simple text or reference. Also called complex data type, composite value, structured data. Examples: an address object with street, city, and zip code; a price specification with amount and currency; a time range with start and end times.
SubscribeAction: The act of forming a unidirectional connection to receive continuous updates from an object or entity. Also called subscribing, following for updates, signing up for notifications. Examples: subscribing to a YouTube channel, signing up for a newsletter, subscribing to a podcast. Distinct from FollowAction, which implies a more reciprocal or social connection. Distinct from RegisterAction, which is a one-time enrollment.
Substance: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.
SubwayStation: A civic structure serving as a stop or terminal for subway or metro trains. Also called metro station, underground station, tube station. Examples: 'Grand Central Terminal', 'London Underground station', 'Tokyo Metro station'.
Suite: A class of luxury accommodations in a hotel or other public lodging, characterized by having multiple rooms. Also called hotel suite, apartment suite, luxury accommodation. Examples: a presidential suite, a family suite with separate living area, a business suite. Distinct from Room, which is a single distinguishable space.
SuperficialAnatomy: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.
SurgicalProcedure: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments, performed for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Also called surgery, operation, medical incision, surgical intervention. Examples: an appendectomy, a knee replacement surgery, a biopsy, a C-section.
SuspendAction: The act of momentarily pausing a device, application, or process. Also called pausing, halting, putting on hold, temporarily stopping. Examples: pausing music playback, suspending a computer process, pausing a timer.
Syllabus: A learning resource that describes the material covered in a course, often broken into sections with time requirements. Also called course outline, curriculum, study plan, course description. Examples: a university course syllabus, a training program outline, a workshop curriculum.
Synagogue: A civic structure serving as a Jewish house of worship and often a center for community activities. Also called Jewish temple, shul, house of prayer. Examples: 'The Great Synagogue of Rome', a local community synagogue.
TVClip: A short segment or part of a television program. Also called TV segment, television excerpt, show clip, broadcast snippet. Examples: a highlight reel from a TV show, a news report segment, a commercial break.
TVEpisode: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.
TVSeason: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.
TVSeries: A creative work series dedicated to television broadcast and associated online delivery, comprising multiple seasons and episodes. Also called television show, TV program, broadcast series. Examples: 'Game of Thrones', 'The Office', 'Stranger Things'.
Table: A web page element used to display data in a structured format of rows and columns. Also called data table, HTML table, grid, tabular data. Examples: a table showing product prices, a table listing sports scores, a table of contents.
TakeAction: The act of gaining ownership of an object from an origin. Also called acquiring, receiving ownership, obtaining, getting. Examples: taking a book from a shelf, taking possession of a purchased item, taking a found object. Distinct from GiveAction, which is the reciprocal act of transferring ownership. Distinct from ReceiveAction, which does not necessarily imply ownership transfer.
TattooParlor: A local business specializing in applying tattoos and often body piercings. Also called tattoo shop, tattoo studio, body art parlor. Examples: 'Ink Master Tattoo', 'Sacred Heart Tattoo', 'Local Tattoo & Piercing'.
Taxi: An intangible service providing a vehicle for hire with a driver for local travel. Also called cab service, taxi ride, hired car service. Examples: booking a taxi through an app, hailing a cab on the street, a pre-booked airport taxi. Distinct from TaxiService, which is the general business or type of service.
TaxiReservation: A reservation for a taxi service, providing details about a specific booking. Also called cab booking, taxi appointment, ride reservation. Examples: a confirmation email for an airport taxi, a pre-booked taxi for a special event, a ride-share reservation.
TaxiService: A local business or service offering vehicles for hire with drivers for local transportation, typically charging based on distance. Also called cab company, taxi provider, ride-hailing service. Examples: 'Yellow Cab Co.', 'Uber', 'Lyft', a local taxi firm. Distinct from Taxi, which refers to an instance of the service or the vehicle itself.
TaxiStand: A civic structure or designated area where taxis wait for passengers. Also called cab stand, taxi rank, hack stand. Examples: a taxi stand at an airport, a designated taxi area outside a hotel, a street corner taxi queue.
Taxon: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).
TechArticle: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.
TelevisionChannel: A unique instance of a television broadcast service on a cable or satellite lineup. Also called TV channel, broadcast channel, cable channel, satellite channel. Examples: 'HBO', 'CNN', 'BBC One', 'ESPN'.
TelevisionStation: A local business or organization that broadcasts television programs. Also called TV broadcaster, broadcast station, local TV channel. Examples: 'WNBC (New York)', 'BBC Television Centre', a local news station.
TennisComplex: A local business or sports activity location featuring multiple tennis courts and related facilities. Also called tennis center, tennis club, tennis facility. Examples: 'Indian Wells Tennis Garden', a community tennis complex, a private tennis club.
Text: A fundamental data type representing a sequence of characters. Also called string, character data, plain text. Examples: "Hello World", "123 Main St", "product description".
TextDigitalDocument: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.
TextObject: A media object representing a text file, which can contain unformatted text or markup like HTML. Also called text file object, digital text file, document media. Examples: a plain text file (.txt), an HTML file, a Markdown document. Distinct from TextDigitalDocument, which is a structured digital document primarily composed of text.
TheaterEvent: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.
TheaterGroup: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.
TherapeuticProcedure: A medical procedure specifically intended to treat a health condition or improve a patient's well-being. Also called medical treatment, therapy, healing procedure. Examples: chemotherapy, physical therapy, surgical removal of a tumor.
Thesis: A scholarly document submitted by a candidate for an academic degree or professional qualification. Also called dissertation, academic paper, research thesis. Examples: a PhD dissertation, a master's thesis, an undergraduate honors thesis.
Thing: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.
Ticket: An intangible item used to grant access or confirm a reservation for an event, travel, or service. Also called pass, voucher, entry permit. Examples: a concert ticket, an airline boarding pass, a bus ticket, a movie ticket.
TieAction: The act of achieving a draw or stalemate in a competitive activity. Also called draw, stalemate, tie game. Examples: two chess players agreeing to a draw, a soccer match ending in a tie, a race where two competitors finish simultaneously.
TierBenefitEnumeration: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.
Time: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".
TipAction: The act of voluntarily giving money to a beneficiary in appreciation for services rendered. Also called gratuity, tipping, giving a tip. Examples: leaving a tip for a waiter, tipping a taxi driver, giving a barber a gratuity.
TireShop: A local business specializing in the sale, repair, and installation of vehicle tires. Also called tire store, auto tire center, wheel shop. Examples: Discount Tire, a local independent tire dealer, a car service center with a tire department.
TouristAttraction: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.
TouristDestination: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.
TouristInformationCenter: A local business providing information and services to tourists. Also called visitor center, tourist office, travel information point. Examples: a city visitor center, a national park information booth, a regional tourism office.
TouristTrip: An itinerary or journey undertaken by visitors for tourism purposes, often involving visits to multiple places of interest. Also called vacation itinerary, travel plan, sightseeing tour. Examples: a two-week European tour, a weekend getaway to a national park, a cruise itinerary.
ToyStore: A local business specializing in the sale of toys and games. Also called toy shop, game store, children's store. Examples: Toys 'R' Us, a local independent toy boutique, a department store's toy section.
TrackAction: The act of monitoring an inanimate object for updates or changes in its location or status. Also called monitoring, tracking, observing. Examples: tracking a package delivery, monitoring a flight's progress, tracking a lost phone.
TradeAction: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.
TrainReservation: A reservation specifically for travel on a commercial train line. Also called train booking, rail reservation, seat booking. Examples: a reservation for a high-speed train, a sleeper car booking, a ticket for a scenic rail journey.
TrainStation: A civic structure serving as a designated stop for trains, where passengers can board or alight. Also called railway station, rail depot, terminal station. Examples: Grand Central Terminal, London King's Cross, a local commuter rail station.
TrainTrip: A journey or itinerary undertaken using a commercial train line. Also called rail journey, train travel, railway trip. Examples: a cross-country train journey, a daily commute by train, a scenic train ride through the mountains.
TransferAction: The act of moving an object, whether animate or inanimate, from one location to another. Also called move, transport, relocate. Examples: transferring funds between bank accounts, moving furniture to a new house, transferring a patient to another hospital.
TravelAction: The act of moving from a starting location to a destination using a specified mode of transport. Also called journey, commute, voyage. Examples: traveling by car from home to work, flying from New York to London, taking a bus to another city.
TravelAgency: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.
TreatmentIndication: A medical indication specifying the appropriate use of a treatment for an underlying health condition or symptom. Also called therapeutic indication, medical use, treatment rationale. Examples: an antibiotic indicated for bacterial infections, a pain reliever indicated for headaches, a specific therapy for cancer.
Trip: A general term for a journey or itinerary involving visits to one or more places. Also called journey, travel, excursion. Examples: a business trip, a family vacation, a day trip to the beach.
TypeAndQuantityNode: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".
UKNonprofitType: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.
URL: A data type representing a Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the address of a resource on the internet. Also called web address, link, internet address. Examples: "https://schema.org", "ftp://example.com/file.zip", "mailto:info@example.com".
USNonprofitType: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.
UnRegisterAction: The act of formally removing oneself from a service, membership, or registration. Also called unsubscribe, deregister, cancel registration. Examples: unregistering from a website, unsubscribing from a newsletter, canceling a gym membership. Distinct from LeaveAction, which implies departing a group or team rather than a service.
UnitPriceSpecification: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".
UpdateAction: The act of managing or changing the state or content of an object. Also called modify, edit, revise. Examples: updating a software application, editing a document, changing a profile picture.
UseAction: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.
UserBlocks: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of blocking another user or content. Also called user block, content block, account block. Examples: a user blocking another user on a social media platform, blocking a specific website, blocking notifications from an app.
UserCheckins: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of checking into a location or event. Also called user check-in, location check-in, event attendance. Examples: a user checking into a restaurant, checking into a concert, marking attendance at a conference.
UserComments: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of posting comments or feedback. Also called user comment, public comment, feedback post. Examples: a user leaving a comment on a blog post, posting a review, providing feedback on a product.
UserDownloads: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of downloading content. Also called user download, content download, file retrieval. Examples: a user downloading a software update, downloading an e-book, saving an image from a website.
UserInteraction: An outdated general type representing any interaction a user has with a web page or content. Also called user activity, user engagement, web interaction. Examples: a user clicking a link, submitting a form, scrolling a page.
UserLikes: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of expressing approval or liking for content. Also called user like, content like, approval. Examples: a user liking a photo on social media, giving a thumbs-up to a video, favoriting an item.
UserPageVisits: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of visiting a web page. Also called page view, web visit, browsing activity. Examples: a user navigating to a product page, visiting a news article, browsing a website.
UserPlays: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of playing media content. Also called user play, media playback, content viewing. Examples: a user playing a video, listening to an audio track, starting a game.
UserPlusOnes: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.
UserReview: A review or critique created by an end-user, such as a consumer or attendee, rather than a professional critic. Also called customer review, consumer feedback, public review. Examples: a customer's product review on an e-commerce site, a diner's restaurant review, an audience member's movie review. Distinct from CriticReview, which is a review written by a professional critic.
UserTweets: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of posting a tweet on Twitter. Also called user tweet, microblog post, social media update. Examples: a user posting a message on Twitter, sharing a link via tweet, replying to another tweet.
VacationRental: A lodging business that offers single properties for rent for limited periods, typically for vacations. Also called holiday rental, short-term rental, vacation home. Examples: an Airbnb apartment, a beach house rental, a cabin in the mountains.
Vehicle: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.
Vein: A type of blood vessel specifically responsible for carrying deoxygenated blood back towards the heart. Also called blood vein, venule, vena. Examples: the jugular vein, the femoral vein, the pulmonary vein.
Vessel: A component of the circulatory system, comprising hollow tubes that transport blood throughout the body. Also called blood vessel, circulatory tube, vascular conduit. Examples: an artery, a vein, a capillary.
VeterinaryCare: A local business or organization providing medical services for animals. Also called vet clinic, animal hospital, veterinary practice. Examples: a local veterinary office, an emergency animal hospital, a mobile vet service.
VideoGallery: A web page designed to display a collection of video content. Also called video collection page, media gallery, video archive. Examples: a YouTube channel page, a news website's video section, a personal video portfolio.
VideoGame: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.
VideoGameClip: A short segment or part of a video game, often used for promotional or highlight purposes. Also called game clip, gameplay footage, video game segment. Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.
VideoGameSeries: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.
VideoObject: A media object representing a video file. Also called video file, digital video, movie clip. Examples: an MP4 video, a YouTube video, a short film.
VideoObjectSnapshot: A specific, byte-for-byte identical version of a video file. Also called exact video copy, identical video file, video instance. Examples: a specific version of a movie file, a particular encoding of a video, a digital master copy of a video.
ViewAction: The act of consuming or perceiving static visual content. Also called look at, observe, gaze upon. Examples: viewing a photograph, looking at a painting, examining a diagram.
VirtualLocation: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.
VisualArtsEvent: An event related to visual arts, such as an exhibition, gallery opening, or art fair. Also called art exhibition, gallery event, visual art show. Examples: a painting exhibition, a sculpture display, a photography festival.
VisualArtwork: A creative work that is primarily visual in nature, such as a painting, sculpture, or photograph. Also called art piece, visual art, artwork. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, a Rodin sculpture, an Ansel Adams photograph.
VitalSign: A measurable physiological function used to assess the most basic body functions and overall health. Also called physiological sign, health indicator, body function measure. Examples: body temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate.
Volcano: A landform, typically a mountain, with a vent through which lava, rock fragments, hot vapor, and gas are ejected. Also called active volcano, dormant volcano, volcanic mountain. Examples: Mount Fuji, Mount Vesuvius, Kilauea.
VoteAction: The act of expressing a preference or choice from a predefined set of options. Also called casting a vote, ballot, election. Examples: voting in a political election, casting a vote for a competition winner, participating in a poll.
WPAdBlock: A specific section of a web page dedicated to displaying advertisements. Also called ad unit, advertising block, banner ad section. Examples: a banner ad at the top of a page, a sidebar ad, an interstitial ad space.
WPFooter: The bottom section of a web page, typically containing copyright information, contact details, and navigation links. Also called page footer, website footer, site bottom. Examples: the copyright notice at the bottom of a website, links to privacy policy and terms of service, social media icons in the footer.
WPHeader: The top section of a web page, typically containing the site's logo, main navigation, and branding elements. Also called page header, website header, site top. Examples: a website's logo and main menu bar, a search bar at the top of a page, a site title.
WPSideBar: A section of a web page positioned to the side of the main content, often used for navigation, advertisements, or supplementary information. Also called page sidebar, side panel, auxiliary column. Examples: a navigation menu on the left side of a blog, a list of related articles in a right sidebar, an ad column.
WantAction: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.
WarrantyPromise: A structured value representing the duration and scope of free services provided for a product's defects or malfunctions. Also called product warranty, guarantee, service promise. Examples: a 1-year manufacturer's warranty, a 90-day repair guarantee, a lifetime parts warranty.
WarrantyScope: An enumeration describing the range of services covered by a warranty in case of product defect or malfunction. Also called warranty coverage, guarantee scope, service level. Examples: "Parts and Labor - Bring In", "Labor - On Site", "Parts Only".
WatchAction: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.
Waterfall: A landform where water flows over a vertical drop or a series of steep drops in the course of a stream or river. Also called cascade, falls, cataract. Examples: Niagara Falls, Victoria Falls, Angel Falls.
WearAction: The act of dressing oneself in clothing or accessories. Also called put on, don, attire oneself. Examples: wearing a coat, putting on shoes, wearing a hat.
WearableMeasurementTypeEnumeration: An enumeration of common measurement types used for wearable products. Also called wearable sizing type, apparel measurement, garment dimension. Examples: "chest circumference", "sleeve length", "inseam".
WearableSizeGroupEnumeration: An enumeration of common size groups or types for wearable products. Also called apparel size group, clothing size type, garment category. Examples: "men's", "women's", "children's", "unisex".
WearableSizeSystemEnumeration: An enumeration of common sizing systems specific to wearable products. Also called apparel sizing system, clothing size standard, garment measurement standard. Examples: "US size system", "EU size system", "UK size system".
WebAPI: An application programming interface that is accessible over web or internet technologies. Also called web service, API, REST API. Examples: the Google Maps API, the Twitter API, a weather data API.
WebApplication: A software application that runs on a web server and is accessed by users via a web browser. Also called web app, online application, browser-based application. Examples: Gmail, Google Docs, Facebook.
WebContent: A general type representing any content accessible via the web, including web pages, websites, and their elements. Also called web content item, online content, digital web asset. Examples: a blog post, an entire website, an image embedded on a page.
WebPage: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.
WebPageElement: A distinct part or component within a web page. Also called page component, web element, UI element. Examples: a navigation menu, an image, a form, a table.
WebSite: A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence. Examples: schema.org, Wikipedia, The New York Times website.
WholesaleStore: A local business that sells goods in large quantities, typically to retailers or other businesses, rather than directly to individual consumers. Also called wholesaler, bulk store, cash and carry. Examples: Costco Business Center, a restaurant supply store, a building materials wholesaler.
WinAction: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.
Winery: A local business that produces wine, often including facilities for grape cultivation, wine production, and tasting. Also called vineyard, wine producer, wine estate. Examples: Robert Mondavi Winery, a local family-owned vineyard, a wine tasting room.
WorkBasedProgram: An educational and employment program structured around work-based learning, aiming to develop occupational competencies. Also called apprenticeship, vocational training, on-the-job training. Examples: an electrician apprenticeship, a culinary arts internship, a software development bootcamp with practical projects.
WorkersUnion: An organization that advocates for the interests of its worker members through collective bargaining and political lobbying. Also called labor union, trade union, industrial union. Examples: United Auto Workers (UAW), National Education Association (NEA), a local plumbers' union.
WriteAction: The act of authoring or creating written creative content. Also called compose, pen, draft. Examples: writing a novel, composing an email, drafting a report.
XPathType: A data type representing an XPath expression, used for navigating XML or HTML documents. Also called XPath expression, XML Path Language, query path. Examples: "/bookstore/book[price>35]", "//title", "id('myElement')".
Zoo: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.
